entries.statement: THE EXECUTION PLANE ORIGINATES EVIDENCE FOR THE INTERACTION-NET DYNAMICS THEMSELVES, rather than the governance plane reconstructing it around the execution plane afterwards. For a frozen fixture, the native C runtime independently emits a chained semantic film whose per-frame pre-state, enabled rule, PLANE, canonical locus and post-state, and whose terminal, are accepted by the existing TRVM-SEMFILM-v1.1 contract WITHOUT normalization or translation of meaning -- the law kernel's own replaySemFilm, imported unmodified, replaying on a fresh runtime of two different allocator classes. @1 SCOPED THIS TO THE APP PLANE and that was the whole frontier: application of a lambda at a tree locus is the part of the calculus a term-rewriting relation already models. @2 IS THE FLOAT PLANE. Enumeration covers the root tree AND EVERY LIVE DUP CELL; loci are canonical in three families -- t: a structural path, d: a DISCOVERY INDEX over live cells, v: a discovery index AND a path into a cell's value -- and AT @3 EVERY RULE OF THE DECLARED POOL HAS A POSITIVE NATIVE WITNESS: APP-LAM, APP-SUP, APP-ERA, DUP-LAM, DUP-SUP=, DUP-SUP!, DUP-ERA, DUP-VAR and DUP-APP. THE TWO ORDERS ARE DIFFERENT ORDERS AND BOTH ARE LOAD-BEARING: the kernel enumerates live cells right-to-left (liveHeap pushes children forward) and INDEXES loci left-to-right (liveDiscoveryOrder pushes them reversed), so one order decides which redex is leftmost and the other decides what number its locus carries; collapsing either onto the other produces a locus that names a real redex which is not the redex that fired. SCOPE, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AND STATED AS REFUSALS: an enumerated rule the emitter cannot fire is REFUSED BY NAME (film-rule-not-implemented) rather than silently skipped, and the pool is enumerated in full regardless of what is implemented -- so that 'no enabled work' cannot mean 'no work of the kinds I implement', which is how a false normal form is written down. THE SCOPE PREDICATE HAS MOVED FOUR TIMES AND EVERY MOVE WAS A CORRECTION (dup PRESENCE, dup ENABLEDNESS, the two ERA rules, and now nothing rule-shaped at all), so the law and its checks name the DURABLE property rather than the current gap. THE ERA RULES CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY DISCOVERY: two purpose-built minimal fixtures -- (* x) is one APP-ERA frame, and !{a,b} = *; lambda z.a is one DUP-ERA frame with a SINGLE live projection, which also exercises the one-sided path through find_projections -- rather than one contrived term that happens to contain both. The conformance corpus contains NO ERA at all, which is why all 24 vectors could agree while two of nine rules had never run natively, and why these had to be BUILT rather than found. AND CANONICAL LOCUS ASSIGNMENT IS INJECTIVE OVER SEMANTIC REDEX IDENTITY: one redex gets at most one canonical locus. The representation makes an alias EXPRESSIBLE -- each findAppRedexes call carries its own visited set, so a node reachable both from the root and from inside a dup value is enumerable under a t: AND a v: locus -- and since the locus is committed into frame_id, two spellings of one transition would be two canonical frame identities for the same pre, rule and post. Identity is PHYSICAL and per-runtime and is therefore NOT a cross-implementation field: each side checks its own. Nothing in the measured fixtures produces an alias; the emitter REFUSES film-locus-alias rather than blessing both spellings, because precedence between them is UNRULED and choosing one silently would decide a rule nobody wrote down. THE ONE-INTERACTION GUARD IS POST-HOC BY RULING AND STAYS SO: it measures what the shipped runtime DID, including any future change inside fire() or whnf(), where a structural pre-check could only measure what is predicted. Its soundness depends on the emitter being FAIL-STOP -- a refusal exits, so a heap mutated before the guard fired never becomes accepted evidence, and a persistent service would need transactional scratch state. The PREDICTION behind it is measured separately rather than left as prose: whnf is INERT on every head class the one classifier admits, at interaction delta 0 AND canonical semantic state unchanged -- the second clause being the one a counter alone would miss, since whnf memoizes a stuck application's reduced head without counting an interaction. No second inline classifier was added to do this; two semantic recognizers can drift. A STEP BUDGET REACHED WHILE WORK REMAINS IS A SEALED TERMINAL AND NO LONGER A REFUSAL -- CHANGED AT B5, AND THE DISTINCTION IT MAKES PORTABLE IS EPISTEMIC. NORMAL_FORM says there is provably no work left; BUDGET_EXHAUSTED says we stopped looking and this much was left. A runtime that cannot separate them cannot be trusted with either, and until v0.5.0 C could originate only the first: reaching a budget produced film-budget-exhausted, which reports the ABSENCE of evidence where the truth is evidence of a partial run. NO NEW CONTRACT WAS INTRODUCED TO DO IT. TRVM-SEMFILM-v1.1 has carried the budget witness since round 6.1, when the round-6B audit falsified v1's terminal by forging a zero-frame BUDGET_EXHAUSTED film over an enabled state that replayed ok with budget and remaining_work outside the commitment entirely; law:film.terminal-witness@1 closed that at the SCHEMA level, and B5 supplies only the ORIGINATOR. C seals {termination, steps, last_frame, final_sem_id, budget, remaining_work, planes}, every field inside film_id and every field RE-DERIVED by replay on two runtime classes. THE TERMINAL IS NOT A TRANSITION: budget describes the state at the moment a further step was DENIED, so no synthetic frame is appended and remaining_work is measured on the state the last real frame left behind. NORMAL_FORM TAKES PRECEDENCE AT THE BOUNDARY, AND THE RULE IS AN ORDERING RATHER THAN A COMPARISON: the terminal is concluded only after a FRESH FULL-POOL ENUMERATION, and an empty pool is a normal form even on the step where the budget ran out. Reading steps == budget as exhaustion would report a completed execution as an abandoned one -- an under-claim, still false, and a proof consumer believing it would keep searching a space that is already closed. AND ONE QUANTITY CROSSES IMPLEMENTATIONS FOR THE FIRST TIME: every native film before this asked the oracle to agree about STATES -- canonical signatures, chains, normal forms. remaining_work is a COUNT, the cardinality of C's fresh full-pool enumeration, and two enumerators that agree about every state they visit can still disagree about how many redexes a state contains; nothing before this round would have noticed. A PARTIAL FILM CARRIES NO NORMAL FORM -- reading one back performs exactly the work the budget denied and reports it beside a terminal saying it was not done -- so normal_form and normal_form_id are ABSENT rather than present-and-to-be-ignored. THE SEMANTIC BUDGET AND THE STORAGE CEILING STAY DISTINCT: --budget N is execution policy and yields evidence, MAXFRAMES is this program's frame array and yields only a refusal, and they coincide numerically at the default -- which is precisely the condition under which two concepts get merged by accident. THE CEILINGS ARE COMPILE-TIME OVERRIDABLE so the guard can be witnessed without moving it: raising a production resource bound to make another production resource bound easier to hit in a test changes the implementation under test to improve the test surface. A defensive resource ceiling is not a semantic refusal and does not owe the same coverage -- mechanism witness and production reachability are two claims and are asserted separately. AND THE RELATION WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS ASSERTED. The C reducer was built with a non-gating --measure formatter and diffed against the independently measured kernel relation over the whole 24-vector corpus and the film fixtures before one conformance assertion existed; NO EXPECTED TABLE APPEARS IN THE EMITTER OR IN THE COMPARATOR, because a conformance theorem whose expected values were transcribed from the other implementation is a TRANSCRIPTION THEOREM. ic32 CANNOT SUBSTITUTE A DUP BY NAME and that cost is representational, not semantic: heap[D] is the cell's value before the rule fires and the other side's substitution afterwards, so a dup is fired from a DEMANDED SIDE and the demanded projection is replaced where it stands, found by a walk over reachable slots that REFUSES (film-projection-not-unique) rather than choosing if it is not unique. The rules fired are ic32's own fire() and app_sup(), unedited. THE TWO TRANSITION SYSTEMS STAY SEPARATE (film_planes): the TRVM calculus film is pre-state -> (rule + locus) -> post-state over the ic32 interaction-net relation, and the derivation evidence relation is DeriveRequest -> evaluate -> DeriveResult; what is shared is HOST INFRASTRUCTURE, not semantics. Film provenance uses the same discipline as derivation.implementation-provenance@4 -- shared ObservedExecutionHost, immutable catalog entry, hash-then-launch, observation keyed over the whole emission -- and REPLAY AND PROVENANCE ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY, because a film can be semantically perfect and its claimed provenance false.
entries.evidence: bridge/film_check.mjs 45/45. B-1: church_exp_2_2 under --budget 3 seals 3 honest frames with remaining_work 4 against a 21-frame full film, replayed on FloatRt and DescFloatRt, and its frames are byte-identical to the unbudgeted film's first three -- the budget TRUNCATED the execution rather than altering it. B-2: --budget 0 seals a zero-frame film, last_frame genesis, remaining_work 1, final state EQUAL to the full film's frame-0 pre-state and no normal_form field -- the exact shape the round-6B audit forged, now GENERATED honestly and judged by the repaired schema. B-3: --budget 20 -> BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with 1 enabled, --budget 21 -> NORMAL_FORM byte-identical to the unbudgeted film. B-4: budgets 0,1,3,10,20,21 all replay on both runtime classes and every one's frames are a prefix of the whole; remaining_work is NOT monotone in the budget (1,2,4,2,1) and is re-derived per film rather than predicted. B-5: on church 4^4 the same term refuses film-locus-path-too-deep unbudgeted and yields an honest 5-frame partial film under --budget 5 -- a storage refusal and an execution terminal out of one term; --budget -1 refuses film-budget-negative. Six resealed terminal forgeries die on their own reasons: inflated work (sem-terminal-work-mismatch), budget lie (sem-budget-mismatch), partial claiming NORMAL_FORM (sem-false-normal-form), wrong final state (sem-terminal-state-mismatch), the COMPLETE film relabelled BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (sem-terminal-work-mismatch, because a quiescent state has no honest remaining_work at all), and pool narrowing. The narrowing is SEARCHED FOR rather than chosen: the pool is cut by exactly one rule that no frame fires and that changes the enabled count, so the attack cannot die on sem-plane-not-permitted at frame 2 while the work arithmetic never runs -- the coincidental-second-occurrence species, caught for the fifth time in this line. B-12: the budget argument is parsed strictly IN THE BINARY -- 11 value cases and 3 argument-shape cases, each answered by name. B5 shipped strtol(arg, NULL, 10), which reads as far as it can and reports nothing about the rest, so --budget abc emitted a valid zero-frame film under a policy nobody set, 3junk parsed as 3, 1.5 truncated, and an overflow had ERANGE ignored so the malformed request came back a COMPLETE 21-frame NORMAL_FORM film -- a confident complete answer to a different question. endptr AND errno now, plus a leading whitespace/'+' check strtol performs in silence; film-budget-invalid for malformed syntax and film-budget-negative kept SEPARATE for a well-formed out-of-range policy, because one code for both cannot say whether to fix a value or fix a spelling. B-13: film-too-many-frames is witnessed by a -DMAXFRAMES=4 LIMITS BUILD refusing on the same fixture the production build completes, with the production ceilings reported by the BINARY (--limits) rather than grepped from the #define, since under an override the source and the program disagree. PRODUCTION REACHABILITY IS STATED SEPARATELY AND WEAKLY, which is the honest form: no term tried reaches the frame array, because MAXPATH binds first on every one of them. B5 first wrote that the frame array COULD NOT be reached -- an unproven universal over every expressible term where the evidence supports only a statement about the terms measured.

entries.statement: AN AUTHORITY CANNOT VALIDATE A SEMANTIC CLAIM USING A PROGRAM RESOLVER SUPPLIED BY THE CLAIMANT. Acceptance takes no proof from its caller — INCLUDING the mapping from semantic identity to semantic program. Re-derivation is only evidence if the authority chose what it re-derived against. The supplier ladder this closes has four rungs and one shape: @1 the caller supplied the implementation LABEL (deriveLocally's third parameter), @2 the registration NAME (registerExecutor), @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence (a launcher's spawn), @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance (accept's registry parameter). Any field a caller controls on the path to a verdict becomes the verdict. AN instanceof CHECK DOES NOT CLOSE IT, and a law that read as 'check the type' would invite exactly the wrong repair: a Proxy satisfies the type, and so does a genuine ProgramRegistry the caller populated with a different program. The repair is OWNERSHIP. The registry is BUILT at the authority's construction from canonical program DATA — ProgramRegistry.bind severs it through canonicalBytes — so the authority owns its semantic oracle rather than sharing an object with whoever built it, and no registry parameter crosses execute() or accept() again. bindProgram remains an explicit authority operation and needs no second rule, because ids are content-bound: teaching the authority const(999) gives it a new id and cannot repoint const(5)'s. So every oracle the authority consults is constructor-time — the World reader (round 17), the semantic registry (here), and the execution host with its immutable catalog (derivation.implementation-provenance@4) — and what a caller supplies is an INTENT and a RESULT TO VALIDATE.
entries.evidence: probe_semoracle_v10_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against a frozen v0.9.0 acceptance — P-4, where an issued request for const(5) is accepted as 999 because the caller passed {verify: () => ({ok:true}), get: () => ({op:'const',value:999})} and the identical result is refused as foreign-result-divergence by the real registry; and P-4b, where the oracle is a GENUINE ProgramRegistry instance holding a different program, which is the case an instanceof check cannot see. 5/5 confined live: no registry parameter on execute or accept, a registry severed at construction so editing the caller's AST afterwards changes nothing, bindProgram unable to repoint an issued id, the whole four-rung surface checked as a set, and the World reader confirmed inert as a parameter too. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20 (case 18: an authority constructed holding no programs answers program-unknown from the far side), derive_battery.mjs 45/45.

entries.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the source core_sem_id, the target term encoding id, the canonical lowering specification and the conformance-vector identity — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DEFERRED AND NAMED: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, inputs arriving at execution, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term, in which case the identity must say so). The first witness uses inputs={} and does not decide it. That decision comes BEFORE the input op, because an unstated variable inside target_term_sem_id is the hidden-identity bug class round 16 exists to prevent.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out.
entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.2.1 and kept as history, superseded, not erased. Revision 1 described the PRE-B1.2 architecture in two places: it printed the LoweringReceipt as {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the domain B1.2 moved onto the template, and it called the parameterized-versus-instantiated question DEFERRED three passes after B1 decided it and B1.1 ruled the framing a false choice. It also described lowering_sem_id as hashing 'the target term encoding id', which was true before the template existed and was the OVER-BINDING B1.2.1 removed. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED: every witness the law cites ran and passed, and the mechanism was correct throughout -- what was stale was the record of what the mechanism does. Cited by ledger items 139 and earlier, which are history and stay as written.

entries.statement: ONE CANONICAL TARGET NORMAL FORM UNDER ONE DECODER DETERMINES ONE STRUCTURAL TRVM OUTCOME, OR A STRUCTURAL DECODE REFUSAL. decode_sem_id identifies the decoder, and decoding is a THIRD relation rather than the tail of lowering: a lowering can be perfect while the decoder reads the normal form wrongly, and a decoder can be perfect while lowering emitted the wrong target term. They fail independently, so they are proved independently. The outcome is STRUCTURAL — {status:'value', value} or {status:'refused', code, locus} — never a rendered reason, which would recreate round 16's 'the identity bound a spelling' one layer up. The decoder reads the CANONICAL SIGNATURE rather than a readback string — the same bytes the 48/48 bridge has agreed on since round 12 — so it cannot be misled by a binder name. §5 compaction is irreversible, so a compacted signature is REFUSED rather than guessed at; that bounds the decodable numerals and the bound is stated rather than discovered.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: decode-is-structural (L0(L1(A(N0,…A(N0,N1)…))) with five applications decodes to {status:'value', value:5}) and decoder-boundary-named (a non-numeral is decode-not-a-church-numeral, a compacted signature is decode-signature-compacted, and 0 and 1 decode — the two shapes that carry no dup). decode_sem_id is distinct from lowering_sem_id and asserted so.

entries.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. Six identities stay distinct and none may be collapsed into another: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs 9/9, the first end-to-end witness: add(const 2, const 3) with inputs={} lowers to one canonical ic32 term whose identity the kernel and ic32_canon agree on; the host launches the catalogued binary and observes the canonical normal form L0(L1(A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,N1))))))); that decodes structurally to {status:'value', value:5}; and its outcome id EQUALS the source evaluator's, whose result was itself accepted by an authority owning every oracle it consulted (derivation.acceptance-authority@1). six-identities-stay-distinct asserts all six values differ. native-film-absent-by-refusal asserts the film emitter REFUSES this exact fixture with film-dup-cell-present — the gap is measured at the fixture the refinement runs on rather than described in the abstract.
entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.2.1 and kept as history. Revision 1 enumerated SIX identities the theorem distinguishes and B1.2 added target_template_sem_id to the chain without adding it here, so the law and the witness that reads it both made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED: the six it listed were genuinely distinct and every case ran -- the claim was true and incomplete, which is why it is record-staleness and not a forgery.

entries.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse.
entries.evidence: lowering.mjs 0.2.0 freezes INPUT_PORT_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, inputsSemId, portSemId and INSTANTIATION_RECEIPT_FIELDS, with instantiate() throwing instantiate-not-implemented. LOWERING_SEM_ID MOVED as a consequence and that is the point: LOWERING_SPEC carries inputs_model, so deciding the model changes the lowering relation, and an id that survived the ruling unchanged would be claiming the decision was not part of the relation. lowering_check.mjs case 'out-of-fragment-refused' asserts decided true, implemented false, three DECLARED falsifiers, and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID distinct from LOWERING_SEM_ID; 9/9 with the refinement witness unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. THE THREE FALSIFIERS ARE DECLARED AND NONE IS WRITTEN -- I-4a allocation-invariance, I-4b source-name-sensitivity, I-4c binding-has-force -- so this law is PROPERTY-TESTED for the DECISION and its refusal surface, and carries NO claim about instantiation behaviour, which does not exist yet. B2 writes the three.

CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id.
entries.evidence: lowering.mjs 0.2.0 freezes INPUT_PORT_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, inputsSemId, portSemId and INSTANTIATION_RECEIPT_FIELDS, with instantiate() throwing instantiate-not-implemented. LOWERING_SEM_ID MOVED as a consequence and that is the point: LOWERING_SPEC carries inputs_model, so deciding the model changes the lowering relation, and an id that survived the ruling unchanged would be claiming the decision was not part of the relation. lowering_check.mjs case 'out-of-fragment-refused' asserts decided true, implemented false, three DECLARED falsifiers, and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID distinct from LOWERING_SEM_ID; 9/9 with the refinement witness unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. THE THREE FALSIFIERS ARE DECLARED AND NONE IS WRITTEN -- I-4a allocation-invariance, I-4b source-name-sensitivity, I-4c binding-has-force -- so this law is PROPERTY-TESTED for the DECISION and its refusal surface, and carries NO claim about instantiation behaviour, which does not exist yet. B2 writes the three. B1.1: lowering_check.mjs case 'semantic-ids-track-semantics-only' asserts that no lifecycle field appears in either semantic projection AND that the projections remain sensitive -- dropping `add` from lowered_ops moves the LOWERING id while changing extra-input semantics or making the source name non-semantic moves the INSTANTIATION id and not lowering's, which is the two-relation ruling measured rather than asserted. Case 'extra-inputs-ignored-by-the-source' runs the real evaluator: input(x) with {x:2, y:999} returns 2, with {} raises program-input-missing. 11/11, and the refinement witness is unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. B1.2: lowering_check.mjs case 'target-template-is-the-pre-allocation-layer' shows the codomain is {t:add,a:{t:church,n:2},b:{t:church,n:3}} with no names and no labels, that emit() reproduces the SAME 129 characters of ic32 the pre-template lowering produced -- so introducing the layer changed neither the executable term nor its outcome -- that a template holding a port is emit-unbound-port rather than emitted, and that structural equality is identity while add(3,2) differs. 12/12, refinement unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED.
entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.2.1 and kept as history. Revision 2 ruled that instantiation carries its own identity and then let that identity name its CODOMAIN in prose, so the executable encoding was a semantic dependency hiding behind the symbol name emit(): changing the add combinator changed the emitted term and moved no id that owns it. The separation of relations was right; the content of one of the two identities was incomplete. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED -- instantiate() has never run.

entries.statement: AN AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT MAY NOT BE SUPPLIED TO THE AUTHORITY THAT WILL TRUST IT. An `instanceof` guard is satisfied by a subclass: two overridden methods — run() that never runs and observationOf() that answers whatever it likes — pass `host instanceof ObservedExecutionHost` while bypassing the catalog, the digest, hash-then-launch and the observation table, all of which remain perfectly correct and perfectly unconsulted. Acceptance then reports implementation_provenance 'observed' for an implementation that never ran. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHAT THE OBJECT IS DESCENDED FROM. THE QUESTION IS WHO BUILT IT. So the repair is not a tighter predicate — Object.getPrototypeOf(host) === ObservedExecutionHost.prototype excludes the subclass and admits a Proxy, and would be derivation.acceptance-authority@1's mistake with a longer expression. The authority takes an EXECUTOR CATALOG, which is data, and constructs the host itself against its module's own class binding, which no caller can substitute. Every authority with such a parameter does the same, because this is a property of the PARAMETER and not of any one class. This is the fifth rung of one ladder: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance, @5 the EXECUTION-AUTHORITY OBJECT itself. Each rung sat in the parameter that had stopped being examined because it was 'obviously infrastructure'. What a caller supplies is an INTENT, a RESULT TO VALIDATE, and — at construction only — the DATA every oracle is built from.
entries.evidence: probe_hostown_v11_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against a frozen v0.10.0 guard — P-5, where a two-method subclass yields ok/validated/fresh_at_check with provenance 'observed', implementation_id impl-c-fake-v1 and executable_artifact_id 'fake-artifact' while run() would throw if it were called; and P-5b, which shows the tighter prototype check would have excluded the subclass and still admitted a Proxy over a genuine host. 4/4 confined live: the host is built from catalog data, both an EvilHost and a GENUINE ObservedExecutionHost are refused in the catalog position because neither is a catalog, editing the caller's catalog object after construction reaches nothing, the authority exposes zero own properties and is frozen with the host behind a #private field, and the five rungs are asserted as a set. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20, derive_battery.mjs 45/45, bridge/film_check.mjs 14/14 with FilmAuthority taking catalog data for the same reason.

entries.statement: UNTRUSTED DATA MUST BE SEVERED BEFORE IT IS VALIDATED, NOT VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS SEVERED. Every untrusted structure that becomes authority state is canonicalised into an OWNED SNAPSHOT exactly once; validation, identity computation and storage then operate only on that snapshot. NO UNOWNED MUTABLE OBJECT IS CONSULTED TWICE ACROSS A TRUST DECISION. A getter is read as many times as it is written, and the reads need not agree. v0.11.0's executor catalog read `entrypoint` four times — typeof, isAbsolute, the entrypoint-inside-closure check, and then the frozen internal entry — so a getter answering honestly for the three validating reads and maliciously for the fourth put an entrypoint OUTSIDE its own hashed closure into the immutable catalog, and the un-hashed executable really ran while acceptance reported the honest closure's digest. ProgramRegistry.bind had the same shape with a milder outcome: it hashed the caller's AST and then cloned it, so the registry could be keyed by const(5)'s identity while holding const(999). THE MILDER OUTCOME IS NOT A DEFENCE. bind fails closed only because verify() recomputes the id from what was stored — a SECOND mechanism catching the first is not the first working, and authorize() will issue a request against the broken id in the meantime. This is the sixth rung, and the first that is not an object: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE, @5 the AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT, @6 MUTABLE DATA READ TWICE. canonicalBytes has refused a capability since v0.1.0; what was not said is that reading THROUGH it twice reintroduces one — the second read IS the capability. The executor catalog is canonical PLAIN DATA only, and a Map is refused: this is a trust boundary whose thesis is that capabilities are not data, and admitting richer JS object forms at it buys nothing.
entries.evidence: probe_snapshot_v12_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against frozen v0.11.0 copies — P-6, where four reads of one getter place an entrypoint outside its own hashed closure into the frozen internal catalog; and P-6b, where three reads split a registry's key from its value. 5/5 confined live: the catalog getter is read EXACTLY ONCE and the honest entrypoint is stored, the same attack driven end to end through the authority runs the honest worker and leaves the evil worker's startup marker absent, the AST getter is read EXACTLY ONCE so key and value agree by construction rather than by a downstream check, a Map and a function-carrying entry are both refused before any field is examined, and the six rungs are asserted as a set.

entries.statement: EVERY AUTHORITY OPERATION CONSUMES EITHER AN AUTHORITY-OWNED OBJECT OR ONE CANONICAL SNAPSHOT MADE AT ENTRY. NO TRUST DECISION AUTHENTICATES ONE READ OF EXTERNAL STATE AND EXERCISES AUTHORITY USING ANOTHER. derivation.owned-snapshot@1 stated this rule for structures BECOMING authority state and was correct; this is the same rule reaching method ARGUMENTS, where it had never been applied. wasIssued(req) hashed one read of every field and proved 'these bytes are the request I issued'; execute() then read the caller's object again for the implementation family, again when the host canonicalised the invocation, and again when the worker structured-cloned it. A request whose program_sem_id answers const(5) to the first read and const(999) to every read after it is therefore ISSUED as one program and EXECUTED as another. Both programs are genuinely in the authority's own registry, so nothing is malformed, no identity is forged and nothing fails closed: acceptance re-derives 999 against 999, finds the provenance of an execution the authority really drove, and returns implementation_provenance 'observed' for a result the authority never authorized. THE SAME RESULT PAIRED WITH THE FROZEN ISSUED REQUEST IS REFUSED as result-program-mismatch, which is what makes this a forgery rather than fail-closed hygiene — the entire difference is the caller's retained ownership. THE REPAIR IS NOT A FRESHER HASH. Hashing again would authenticate a second read and leave a third. The issuance table keeps the REQUEST and not merely its identity, because a table of hashes can answer 'were these bytes issued?' and cannot answer 'what did I issue?', and every method that needed the second question had no choice but to re-read the caller; wasIssued() returns that owned request and execute() and accept() read it. THE RESULT SIDE WAS CLOSED IN THE SAME ROUND, ONE ARGUMENT TO THE RIGHT, without waiting for its own witness: `res` was consulted by six checks in sequence, and a caller who cannot vary the request while it is validated can still vary the result. Seven rungs, one shape — LABEL, NAME, ACTION, SEMANTIC ORACLE, AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT, MUTABLE DATA READ TWICE, MUTABLE DATA AUTHENTICATED ONCE — and @6 and @7 are one rule at two moments: validate X then store X', authenticate X then act with X'. The mechanism is one exported ownCanonical() called at the top of every method taking a non-root data argument, and the enforcement is a battery case that enumerates the authority's entrypoints and fails when any argument is read more than once per field, because a law applied only where a witness has been written is a law with the reach of its witnesses. AND THE OBLIGATION BELONGS TO THE ENTRYPOINT, NOT TO ITS POLITEST CALLER. ObservedExecutionHost.run() keyed the observation over canonicalBytes(invocation) and then handed the same live object to the transport, so an invocation honest on read 1 and hostile on read 2 was KEYED under one request and EXECUTED as another, leaving a true-looking observation for an execution that did not happen — in the table round 23 built precisely so that relabelling would move the key. That path is unreachable through DerivationAuthority.execute, whose invocation is assembled from owned parts; the host is nonetheless exported, FilmAuthority and lowering_check drive it directly, and it writes the observation table, so it is an authority operation carrying the rule itself (P-7c). THE REUSABLE VALIDATORS CARRY THE SAME OBLIGATION AT THEIR OWN EDGE. checkRequest, checkIntent, checkResult, deriveLocally and validateForeignResult reread their arguments field by field — one checkRequest call over a Proxy-wrapped request touched ownKeys 2, getOwnPropertyDescriptor 10, getPrototypeOf 1, get 13 and has 1 — so 'a pure function over data the caller already owns' is the second half of a sentence whose first half was a precondition nothing enforced. The implementations are named ...Owned and the precondition is mechanical inside the authority, which passes only issued/ownRes/ownIntent; the exported names snapshot once and delegate, so a second authority built on them cannot recreate P-7 without writing new trust logic. This is an API-boundary hazard predicted by the law, not a false verdict, and it is deliberately not numbered as a rung. AND HISTORICAL FACT IS NOT A FUNCTION OF CURRENT CONFIGURATION. Acceptance rebuilt the invocation it asked the observation table about out of this.#registry.image(), so bindProgram() — an explicit, legitimate authority operation — grew that image and made the provenance of an earlier genuine execution vanish: execute(A), accept -> observed, bindProgram(B), accept the same request and result -> implementation-provenance-unavailable. It fails closed and forges nothing, and it is still wrong, because unrelated future installation must not erase the evidence of what previously ran. execute() now records the canonical invocation bytes THE HOST KEYED, acceptance looks those up, and the records are a list because the same request run before and after a bind is two genuinely different invocations and both happened; observations across them are MERGED rather than first-hit, for the round-24 reason that reporting one launch as though it were the only one overclaims. DECLARED OPEN: object-form canonicalisation MAY INVOKE JavaScript accessor and Proxy behaviour while capturing its snapshot — reading {get x(){}} executes a function, and a Proxy runs ownKeys/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/getPrototypeOf/has/get traps during serialisation. What is established is that no such behaviour SURVIVES the snapshot or participates in any later authority decision, measured as a full-trap surface equal to exactly one ownCanonical traversal. The stronger property — no hostile same-realm code executes at ingestion at all — is unreachable for any API whose boundary is an arbitrary JavaScript object, and needs a serialized-wire boundary (canonical text -> authority-owned parser -> data), which is not built. Relatedly, the read-count enumeration is a REGRESSION DETECTOR AND NOT A TERMINATING PROOF: Object.keys(x) twice leaves an accessor's read count at zero while touching the object twice, so a field-read counter sees only the `get` category and the meta-operation instrument covers the rest.
entries.evidence: probe_reread_v13_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against frozen v0.12.0 copies of execute() and accept() — the authority issues psem-82eee05e… (const 5), executes psem-3b198d80… (const 999), the native worker returns 999, and acceptance of that result under a fresh time-varying request returns {ok:true, validated:true, implementation_provenance:'observed'} while the frozen issued request refuses it as result-program-mismatch. 5/5 confined live: a time-varying request is read EXACTLY ONCE by execute() and the program that runs is the one authorized; acceptance reads a time-varying request once and a time-varying result once; wasIssued() returns the deep-frozen issued request and a stranger authority still gets grant-not-issued-by-this-authority and no request; a function-carrying result, a ProgramRegistry in the request slot and a closure-carrying intent each die at the entry rather than halfway through; and the ladder is one frozen record of seven rungs. derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'every-entrypoint-reads-its-argument-once' enumerates nine entrypoints and measures reads against a one-read-per-field floor: 7/7, 1/1, 11/11, 11/11, 11/11, 18/18, 11/11, 18/18, 2/2. Reintroducing the defect in execute() alone moves that to 33/11 and the case names the offending entrypoint. P-7c: 3/3 frozen breaches and 6/6 live confinements in the same probe — the frozen v0.2.1 read ordering splits the keyed request from the executed one, and the live host reads its invocation exactly once, answers 5 for the request it keyed, and holds the observation under the bytes that ran and not under the ones that did not. derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'meta-operations-stop-at-one-traversal' hands twelve entrypoints — including the reusable exports — a RECURSIVELY Proxy-wrapped argument counting ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, getPrototypeOf, has and get, and requires each to equal a single ownCanonical traversal exactly (e.g. wasIssued/req gOPD:11 get:11 getPrototypeOf:6 ownKeys:6).

entries.statement: MULTIPLICITY MUST PRESERVE CORRELATION. EVIDENCE FIELDS THAT VARY TOGETHER MAY NOT BE INDEPENDENTLY COLLAPSED INTO SINGULAR SUMMARIES. Round 24 established that the observation key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it, and made executor_sessions plural so that one id would stop being reported as though it named the launch in hand. It left executable_artifact_id singular over that same plural list, taking list[0]. Those two fields are not independent. Run one issued request, append a comment to derive_worker.mjs, run it again: the host honestly observes S1 -> artifact A -> 5 and S2 -> artifact B -> 5, and the old shape reported executable_artifact_id A beside executor_sessions [S1, S2], implying both sessions ran A. Nothing false is accepted and no execution is invented -- both happened and both produced these exact request/result bytes -- so this is not a forgery but a PROVENANCE SHAPE defect, and it matters because the two artifact versions may differ arbitrarily and coincide only on this request's result. It is the database error of selecting one column from the first row and another column from all rows and presenting the pair as a record. THE TUPLE IS THE UNIT: observations are grouped by the (implementation_family_id, executable_artifact_id) that actually co-occurred, carrying the sessions that ran it, and every singular field is DERIVED -- emitted only when genuinely unique and null otherwise, which is what the family id has done since round 24 and what the artifact id should have done alongside it. Provenance is RELATIONAL: family <-> artifact <-> session, not three unrelated sets. There is ONE summariser, in the host, used by the host and by the authority that merges across invocations, because the first version of that merge rewrote the same correlation bug one level up.
entries.evidence: derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'multiplicity-preserves-correlation' drives two authority-driven executions of ONE issued request across a change to derive_worker.mjs's bytes -- same catalog, same family, same request, same result -- and requires acceptance to report two correlated execution_observations, executable_artifact_id null because it is not unique, each session still attached to the artifact that actually ran it, and executor_sessions of length 2. Restoring the list[0] form fails the case. The witness restores the worker's bytes in a finally block, so the artifact tree is unchanged whether it passes or throws.

entries.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the LOWERING SEMANTICS alone: the source core_sem_id, the id of its CODOMAIN encoding (TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, and NOT the executable encoding, which is instantiation's codomain), the per-op lowering map, the refusal vocabulary lower() can actually produce, and totality on the fragment — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DECIDED AT B1 AND BUILT AT B1.2, and the earlier framing was wrong: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term) was a FALSE CHOICE. The template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed, so there are TWO relations with two identities and lowering's codomain is the TEMPLATE. This statement said DEFERRED for three passes after the decision, and printed the pre-B1.2 receipt shape for one -- while grid_check REQUIRED the deferred wording, which turns a check into a ratchet holding a stale record in place. See derivation.instantiation-identity@3. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. Each list now belongs to the record that owns it, and every name lowering claims is driven to a refusal by the witness.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out. B1.2.1 adds emit-is-not-a-hidden-relation (three emitter mutations move the instantiation id and not lowering's; two per-op rule mutations move lowering's and not instantiation's; a template-grammar mutation moves both and the template-encoding id; every name in refusal_semantics is driven to a refusal) and chain-identities-stay-distinct, whose set is DERIVED from REFINEMENT_CHAIN rather than hand-typed.
entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B2, when the relation it describes became EXECUTABLE, and kept as history. Revision 2 described a decided-and-unbuilt architecture; nothing in it was false and no verdict rested on behaviour that did not exist -- instantiate() had never run. What changed is that the claims are now witnessed rather than declared.

entries.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. THE CHAIN'S IDENTITIES STAY DISTINCT AND NONE MAY BE COLLAPSED INTO ANOTHER, and the chain is DECLARED rather than counted in prose: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id, of which the last two of the first five are DECLARED AND NOT EXERCISED until instantiation is built. THIS SENTENCE SAID 'SIX' AND OMITTED target_template_sem_id for the whole of B1.2, the pass that introduced it as an independently identified semantic object -- so the law, and the anti-collapse witness reading it, made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain and were green throughout. The enumeration now lives in REFINEMENT_CHAIN with an exercised flag per node and the witness DERIVES its set from it, because a hand-typed count drifting from the thing it counts is a species this tree has now caught in a law count, a case count, a rung count and here. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid.

entries.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged.

Nothing about the runtime was wrong: the RELATION misbound its own input identity. That is derivation.entry-snapshot@1 arriving in the compiler layer, and the repair is the same mechanism: ONE canonical snapshot of BOTH arguments at entry, everything downstream reading the snapshot. THE INVARIANT: the bytes inputs_sem_id identifies are exactly the bytes from which every substituted value was derived. (2) A CLOSED VOCABULARY OF BARE NAMES STILL HIDES SEMANTICS. B2's rule table named predicates and transforms and bound each name to a JavaScript function, so redefining `integer` from Number.isInteger to always-true made const(1.5) lower successfully instead of refusing WITH LOWERING_SEM_ID UNCHANGED, and `identity` could have been made to normalize a source input name, silently undoing the port ruling. The vocabulary stays CLOSED and its DEFINITIONS are now data hashed into the relation; a rule may not name a predicate by JavaScript reference or by a bare string resolved elsewhere, and when the core exports reusable semantic predicates a rule references one by its predicate_sem_id. The kind interpreter is trusted code like canonicalBytes: what has been removed is the rule LANGUAGE's ability to hide meaning. (3) THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER FIRED, AND B2 TRIPPED ALL FOUR CONDITIONS AT ONCE. emit() is exported and independently reused; I-4a is a theorem about EMISSION ALONE, comparing two emitters over one template; the executable encoding carries its own content identity and an alternate emitter was deliberately run against it; and instantiate() RETURNED the closed template to its caller. So INSTANTIATION ENDS AT A CLOSED TEMPLATE and EMISSION is a third relation with EMISSION_SEM_ID: program -(lowering)-> template -(instantiation + inputs)-> CLOSED TEMPLATE -(emission)-> target term -(native film)-> normal form -(decode)-> outcome. The closed template carries its OWN IDENTITY DOMAIN, ctmpl- against tmpl-, EVEN WHERE ITS BYTES EQUAL AN OPEN TEMPLATE'S: for a program with no inputs the two structures are byte-identical and they are not the same thing -- one is what the COMPILER produced and the other is what an INVOCATION closed, and sharing an id would make 'this was instantiated' and 'this needed no instantiation' indistinguishable. THE SPLIT MADE THE VERIFIERS CLEANER, which is an argument for it rather than a consequence: verifying instantiation needs NO runtime canonicaliser at all, because the relation now ends at a structure the module owns, and only emission needs one -- which it TAKES AS A PARAMETER, because the module that defines a relation must not also choose the oracle that judges it. Both verifiers are production functions; at B2 the only implementation of 'does this receipt hold?' lived in the test suite, and a relation whose verification procedure exists only in its own tests is a relation nobody else can check.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out. B1.2.1 adds emit-is-not-a-hidden-relation (three emitter mutations move the instantiation id and not lowering's; two per-op rule mutations move lowering's and not instantiation's; a template-grammar mutation moves both and the template-encoding id; every name in refusal_semantics is driven to a refusal) and chain-identities-stay-distinct, whose set is DERIVED from REFINEMENT_CHAIN rather than hand-typed. entries.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term.
