entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs 13/13, the first end-to-end witness: add(const 2, const 3) with inputs={} lowers to one canonical ic32 term whose identity the kernel and ic32_canon agree on; the host launches the catalogued binary and observes the canonical normal form L0(L1(A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,N1))))))); that decodes structurally to {status:'value', value:5}; and its outcome id EQUALS the source evaluator's, whose result was itself accepted by an authority owning every oracle it consulted (derivation.acceptance-authority@1). six-identities-stay-distinct asserts all six values differ. native-film-absent-by-refusal asserts the film emitter REFUSES this exact fixture with film-dup-cell-present — the gap is measured at the fixture the refinement runs on rather than described in the abstract. At B1.2.1 the anti-collapse case is chain-identities-stay-distinct: it requires a value for every node REFINEMENT_CHAIN marks exercised, fails if a declared node is not wired into the witness, and NAMES the unexercised ones in its output -- a node silently absent and a node declared absent being the difference between a stale instrument and a scoped one. B2: every node of REFINEMENT_CHAIN is now exercised -- the witness reaches native code THROUGH instantiate(), so instantiation_sem_id and inputs_sem_id stopped being declared architecture. B2.1: the chain is ELEVEN nodes, all exercised — closed_template_sem_id and emission_sem_id joined it when the split fired, and the derived anti-collapse set grew with it without anyone editing a count. I-4c is now FILM-EVIDENCED: the x + (x + y) term emits a 12-frame all-APP-LAM film terminating in NORMAL_FORM which the kernel replays on two runtime classes, so the INPUT refinement witness carries the grade the no-input one has had since round 26. This does NOT advance the runtime frontier: every frame is APP-LAM at tree loci, and the six DUP-* rules, the d:/v: loci and BUDGET_EXHAUSTED remain exactly as unexercised.

entries.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled -- CLOSED AT B3.2 BY film.native-emission@2, AND NOT BY THIS FIXTURE, which is the distinction worth keeping: the lowered add still fires no dup rule and still emits the same six APP-LAM frames, so what changed is the EMITTER's reach and not this witness's coverage. At v0.2.0 those six frames were the limit of what could be filmed; at v0.3.0 they are a fact about the term. A refinement witness whose grade improves because a neighbouring capability grew, without its own fixture exercising the new capability, has not gained evidence -- and saying so is the only thing that keeps the two apart. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. THE CHAIN'S IDENTITIES STAY DISTINCT AND NONE MAY BE COLLAPSED INTO ANOTHER, and the chain is DECLARED rather than counted in prose: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id, of which the last two of the first five are DECLARED AND NOT EXERCISED until instantiation is built. THIS SENTENCE SAID 'SIX' AND OMITTED target_template_sem_id for the whole of B1.2, the pass that introduced it as an independently identified semantic object -- so the law, and the anti-collapse witness reading it, made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain and were green throughout. The enumeration now lives in REFINEMENT_CHAIN with an exercised flag per node and the witness DERIVES its set from it, because a hand-typed count drifting from the thing it counts is a species this tree has now caught in a law count, a case count, a rung count and here. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. AND instantiate() MAY NOT MINT THE IDENTITY OF ITS OWN OUTPUT: an instantiator that emitted bytes and certified their semantic id would produce the artifact and the certificate from one source, so a wrong emission would carry a matching id and verify against itself. The kernel canonicalises the bytes; the receipt is built around that id; verification RE-INSTANTIATES and RE-CANONICALISES independently rather than asking the instantiator to agree with itself. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged. CORRECTED AND SPLIT AT B2.1. THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST IS A DEFECT. (1) THE INSTANTIATOR MAY NOT READ ITS ARGUMENTS TWICE. B2's instantiate() read the caller's inputs once to BIND values into the term and again to compute inputs_sem_id, so a getter answering 2 and then 999 produced a term meaning x=2 beside an identity committing to {x:999} -- an application record asserting 'these inputs were {x:999}' above 'this term represents x=2'. Nothing about the runtime was wrong: the RELATION misbound its own input identity. That is derivation.entry-snapshot@1 arriving in the compiler layer, and the repair is the same mechanism: ONE canonical snapshot of BOTH arguments at entry, everything downstream reading the snapshot. THE INVARIANT: the bytes inputs_sem_id identifies are exactly the bytes from which every substituted value was derived. (2) A CLOSED VOCABULARY OF BARE NAMES STILL HIDES SEMANTICS. B2's rule table named predicates and transforms and bound each name to a JavaScript function, so redefining `integer` from Number.isInteger to always-true made const(1.5) lower successfully instead of refusing WITH LOWERING_SEM_ID UNCHANGED, and `identity` could have been made to normalize a source input name, silently undoing the port ruling. The vocabulary stays CLOSED and its DEFINITIONS are now data hashed into the relation; a rule may not name a predicate by JavaScript reference or by a bare string resolved elsewhere, and when the core exports reusable semantic predicates a rule references one by its predicate_sem_id. The kind interpreter is trusted code like canonicalBytes: what has been removed is the rule LANGUAGE's ability to hide meaning. (3) THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER FIRED, AND B2 TRIPPED ALL FOUR CONDITIONS AT ONCE. emit() is exported and independently reused; I-4a is a theorem about EMISSION ALONE, comparing two emitters over one template; the executable encoding carries its own content identity and an alternate emitter was deliberately run against it; and instantiate() RETURNED the closed template to its caller. The condition that settles it is the second: once two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong, which is exactly what a merged relation does. So INSTANTIATION ENDS AT A CLOSED TEMPLATE and EMISSION is a third relation with EMISSION_SEM_ID: program -(lowering)-> template -(instantiation + inputs)-> CLOSED TEMPLATE -(emission)-> target term -(native film)-> normal form -(decode)-> outcome. The closed template carries its OWN IDENTITY DOMAIN, ctmpl- against tmpl-, EVEN WHERE ITS BYTES EQUAL AN OPEN TEMPLATE'S: for a program with no inputs the two structures are byte-identical and they are not the same thing -- one is what the COMPILER produced and the other is what an INVOCATION closed, and sharing an id would make 'this was instantiated' and 'this needed no instantiation' indistinguishable. Two receipts, each verified by recomputation of its OWN relation and neither filmed: InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, closed_template_sem_id} and EmissionReceipt {closed_template_sem_id, emission_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. THE SPLIT MADE THE VERIFIERS CLEANER, which is an argument for it rather than a consequence: verifying instantiation needs NO runtime canonicaliser at all, because the relation now ends at a structure the module owns, and only emission needs one -- which it TAKES AS A PARAMETER, because the module that defines a relation must not also choose the oracle that judges it. Both verifiers are production functions; at B2 the only implementation of 'does this receipt hold?' lived in the test suite, and a relation whose verification procedure exists only in its own tests is a relation nobody else can check. B7 CARRIES `sub` THROUGH THE WHOLE CHAIN AND ADDS A SECOND DIRECTION TO THE CLAIM. The emitting side is the same eleven-node chain at the same grade -- sub(const 5, const 2) lowers, instantiates, emits 165 bytes of real predecessor structure, is filmed natively over 96 frames spanning APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM and DUP-SUP= with 66 dup-plane loci, replayed by the kernel on two runtime classes, normalised, decoded to 3, and agreed with by the source evaluator. THIS IS THE FIRST REFINEMENT WITNESS THAT IS ALSO A DUP-PLANE TERM: add(const 2, const 3) films six APP-LAM frames at tree loci and fires no dup rule at all, so until B7 the refinement chain and the runtime frontier were exercised by different fixtures. THE ASSOCIATION PAIR SHOWS THE TEMPLATE SHAPE IS SEMANTIC: (7-2)-1 and 7-(2-1) share three literals and one operator, lower to different templates, emit different terms and decode to 4 and 6 -- so nothing between source and target flattens, reassociates, or pre-inverts an operand pair. The ONE inversion the target needs (the subtrahend is the numeral applied) lives inside emit() and nowhere else. AND THE OTHER DIRECTION IS NOW PART OF THE CLAIM RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: three unrepresentable programs LOWER and INSTANTIATE and are refused only at EMISSION as emit-sub-underflow, while the source evaluator returns -1, 1 and -3. That is a CODOMAIN refusal -- source language properly contains the representable target fragment -- and NOT refusal preservation, which remains DECLARED OPEN and untouched. REFINEMENT_SCOPE.representable_only records the distinction so the two cannot be confused later. AND B7 TRIPPED A RATCHET IN THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN IN THE RECORD: two cases drove lower-unsupported-op with a hard-typed {op:"sub"} and both FAILED the moment sub lowered. The driver is now DERIVED from CORE_SPEC.ops minus IMPLEMENTED_LOWERED_OPS minus the read family, with a null driver counted as a FAILURE rather than a skip -- repointing it at the next unlowered op would have rebuilt the identical trap for whichever round widens next.

entries.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. entries.statement: HISTORY MAY BE PINNED. LIVE STATE MUST BE DERIVED. An instrument whose intended subject is the LIVE, CURRENT or CANONICAL state may not LOCATE or CHARACTERISE that subject with a literal belonging to one phase -- a revision number, a version string, a count, or a boolean polarity. An instrument whose subject genuinely IS history may and SHOULD pin it, because deriving a historical subject makes it stop testing history; that case declares itself with an explicit exemption carrying a reason. THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENCE, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS A GUARD OF ITS OWN. A phase-pinned case is not VACUOUS -- a superseded revision still exists, so the mutation really changes a file -- and its declared TARGET still matches, and the clean baseline is still clean. Every other apparatus check passes. The case has simply stopped testing the thing it names, and the two available outcomes are a failure that reads like an engine defect, or nothing at all when a neighbouring assertion happens to catch the mutation anyway. FOUR INSTANCES IN TWO ROUNDS EARNED THIS LAW, and they are recorded rather than summarised because the shape is easier to recognise than to define: (1) grid_check required lowering_spike.inputs_model.implemented === false, correct while the port was open and, once B2 built it, the mechanism preventing the record from admitting the port had closed -- four passes stale; (2) the negative case guarding it forged implemented=True and expected 'must stay false', so the BATTERY enforced the stale value and 298/298 stayed green over a record contradicting the code; (3) grid_check selected the canonical film law by revision === 3, hand-edited on every supersession; (4) three battery cases selected revision == 3, and when @4 became canonical they went on mutating a superseded revision nothing asserts over and reported their own forgeries as UNCAUGHT. THE RULE IS NOT 'NO LITERALS IN EXPECTATIONS', which would be too blunt: implementation-provenance@1 must stay on the record AS a false claim, and film.native-emission@1 carries a readback record no later revision repeats. Those are correct BECAUSE they are pinned. The distinguishing question is what the instrument's SUBJECT is, not whether a number appears in it. AND THE CATALOGUE STAYS BOUNDED. This is the TENTH species in harness_selftest, added because the class repeated and not because it might; the guard is a narrow lint over the two negative runners, not a general analyzer for every way a test can be written badly. Ten, and then stop until an eleventh actually appears.

Harness 14/14.

entries.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. TWO PROPERTIES THAT LOOK CONTRADICTORY ARE PROVED SEPARATELY. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it.

entries.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. THREE IDENTITIES FORM A LADDER, AND EMISSION PROVES THE MIDDLE ONE. exact emitted BYTES --quotient alpha-renaming and label SPELLING--> target_term_sem_id --execute, normalise, decode--> outcome_sem_id. Different bytes may share a target_term_sem_id; different target_term_sem_ids may share an outcome_sem_id; this battery demonstrates BOTH. AND THE LADDER IS STATED WHERE NOTHING HASHES IT. Until B6.3 the three-grade account above lived inside TARGET_ENCODING as `three_grades`, so REWORDING IT moved TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID and, through it, EMISSION_SEM_ID, while every emitted byte and every conformance case stood still. It is an accurate account of the PROOF ARCHITECTURE and not a property of the executable encoding -- B1.1's defect family with EXPLANATORY rather than governance prose in the hashed seat -- and it now lives in three unhashed places: lowering.mjs's header, emission_conformance.mjs's header, and this law. The same edit removed a B6-era attribution sentence from label_semantics, because WHO ruled a thing is provenance and a citation inside a hashed record re-identifies the encoding the day the citation is corrected. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECEIPT IS EXACT: EmissionReceipt carries no byte digest, so it does not and MUST NOT claim 'these exact bytes were produced'. It proves that the closed template maps, under this emission semantics, to this canonical target-term identity. If byte reproducibility ever needs proving it belongs beside executable_artifact_id as PROVENANCE, not inside a semantic relation whose own codomain deliberately erases the spelling. AND A BYTE CLAIM IS RELATIVE TO THREE THINGS, NOT TWO. @3 wrote E-1b as `same closed template + same emitter profile -> same bytes` and the {f0,f1} -> {q0,q1} mutation refutes it directly: the bytes moved on 6 of 9 fixtures and the profile id -- the theorem's entire stated precondition -- stood still. A PROFILE IS CONFIGURATION AND CONFIGURATION DOES NOT BIND AN IMPLEMENTATION THAT DECLINES TO READ IT. So E-1b is scoped to `same closed template + same emitter PROFILE + same emitter ARTIFACT -> same exact bytes`, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_ARTIFACT_ID, which hashes the source text of every function that produces bytes. IT IS PROVENANCE AND IT IS ALLOWED TO OVERMOVE: a comment inside emit() moves it, which would be B1.1's defect in a semantic id and is exactly right for an artifact identity whose claim is `these exact implementation bytes`. THREE KINDS OF IDENTITY, AND CONFLATING ANY TWO IS A DEFECT THIS LINE HAS NOW PAID FOR SEPARATELY: semantic relation identity (moves only when meaning moves), serializer CONFIGURATION identity (moves when a knob moves, never for a reword), serializer IMPLEMENTATION identity (moves for any edit to the code). E-1a is unchanged and still says nothing about bytes. B6 framed this as a PAIR -- canonical determinism against semantic equivalence -- which is right at the top and hides that target_term_sem_id sits BETWEEN bytes and meaning rather than at either end. AND THE TWO ADVERSARIES ARE DIFFERENT ANIMALS, which B6 fused. CANONICAL DRIFT (E-F1): same closed template, same relation id, a changed claim about the target term, therefore REFUSE -- it needs NO semantic equivalence and therefore applies to every fixture. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE (E-8): different target_term_sem_id, SAME meaning -- it requires a real equivalence and is applicable only where the fragment supplies one. Fused, the canonical-drift falsifier would lose its adversary the moment a non-commutative operator arrived, for a reason having nothing to do with what it proves. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it. AND THE PROJECTION NOW MATCHES THE ONTOLOGY, WHICH AT @2 IT DID NOT. B6.1 ruled label spelling nonsemantic in prose while EMISSION_SEM_ID went on hashing the allocation policy, and the resulting defect was INVERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: editing the PROSE describing the counter moved EMISSION_SEM_ID while bytes and target terms were untouched, and editing the ACTUAL counter inside emit() changed the bytes on 7 of 9 fixtures while EMISSION_SEM_ID stood still. The id was bound to a DESCRIPTION of the policy rather than to the policy -- B1.1's finding that governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when reworded, recurring in the one field B6.1 had corrected the wording of without moving. THE SPLIT: the SEMANTIC target-term encoding commits to Church and add structure, to DUP label EQUALITY AND FRESHNESS relationships, to the alpha and label-permutation quotient, and to the semantic refusals. The CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE commits to counter start, allocation traversal, binder spelling and exact representative bytes, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID, which NO semantic identity cites. THE PROFILE IS INTERPRETED AND NOT DESCRIBED: emit() reads label_counter_start from it, exactly as lower() reads op_lowering_rules since B2.1, so the policy cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving the profile id. AND AT B6.2 THAT WAS TRUE OF ONE FIELD OUT OF SIX, WHICH IS THE DEFECT RECURRING INSIDE ITS OWN FIX. The profile shipped one interpreted knob beside five English sentences and hashed all six. Rewording binder_spelling moved the profile id while bytes, target terms and all eleven cases were untouched; changing the ACTUAL binder spelling from {f0,f1} to {q0,q1} moved the bytes on 6 of 9 fixtures while the profile id stood still; and `label_order` -- `depth-first, operands in declared field order` -- is true of TWO allocation orders that emit different bytes on 5 of 9, so the sentence did not even DETERMINE what it was hashed to identify. THE RULE B6.3 APPLIES: A HASHED FIELD IS A VALUE THE CODE READS OR IT IS NOT HASHED. label_counter_start, label_alloc_order (a closed enum, unknown values a NAMED refusal) and binder_names (the actual names, not a description of how they are chosen) are read by emit(); no hashed value contains a space, so prose has no field it could occupy, which is the structural form TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING.no_names_no_labels uses rather than a promise to keep sentences out. The prose is intact and unhashed in CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_NOTES. An English sentence beside a hard-coded constant is two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed, which is precisely how the field came to be false in both directions. AND NO ALLOCATION POLICY IS HASHED UPSTREAM EITHER: TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING named a counter start, so changing an emitter's allocation re-cut the TEMPLATE, LOWERING and INSTANTIATION identities -- a layer whose whole claim is that no allocation exists in it cannot also commit to how one is performed two layers down. THE RECEIPT IS UNCHANGED AND STAYS THAT WAY: no byte digest is added. Exact bytes are PROVENANCE and belong beside executable_artifact_id.

THE WHOLE PASS IS BYTE-PRESERVING -- emitted bytes identical on 9/9 fixtures against B6.2 -- which is what makes it a projection correction rather than an emitter change; TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, LOWERING_SEM_ID and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID are byte-identical too, and the B6.2 xenc, esem and profile ids are kept in SUPERSEDED_EXPLANATORY_PROSE_SEM_IDS with which two moves were corrections and which one was a redefinition named rather than left to a reader diffing two packs. Emission 13/13 over 9 fixtures. B6.3.1 CLOSES THE ARTIFACT CLOSURE AND GENERALISES E-8, ON TWO MEASUREMENTS TAKEN BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. The table mutation reproduces exactly as reported: bytes 5/9, target terms 0/9, and cemp, cema, xenc, esem, tenc, lsem, isem ALL unchanged -- add(2,3) moving from operand labels &0,&1,&2 with the add at &3 to the add at &0 with operands &1,&2,&3. entries.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. THREE IDENTITIES FORM A LADDER, AND EMISSION PROVES THE MIDDLE ONE. exact emitted BYTES --quotient alpha-renaming and label SPELLING--> target_term_sem_id --execute, normalise, decode--> outcome_sem_id. Different bytes may share a target_term_sem_id; different target_term_sem_ids may share an outcome_sem_id; this battery demonstrates BOTH. AND THE LADDER IS STATED WHERE NOTHING HASHES IT. Until B6.3 the three-grade account above lived inside TARGET_ENCODING as `three_grades`, so REWORDING IT moved TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID and, through it, EMISSION_SEM_ID, while every emitted byte and every conformance case stood still. It is an accurate account of the PROOF ARCHITECTURE and not a property of the executable encoding -- B1.1's defect family with EXPLANATORY rather than governance prose in the hashed seat -- and it now lives in three unhashed places: lowering.mjs's header, emission_conformance.mjs's header, and this law. The same edit removed a B6-era attribution sentence from label_semantics, because WHO ruled a thing is provenance and a citation inside a hashed record re-identifies the encoding the day the citation is corrected. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECEIPT IS EXACT: EmissionReceipt carries no byte digest, so it does not and MUST NOT claim 'these exact bytes were produced'. It proves that the closed template maps, under this emission semantics, to this canonical target-term identity. If byte reproducibility ever needs proving it belongs beside executable_artifact_id as PROVENANCE, not inside a semantic relation whose own codomain deliberately erases the spelling. AND A BYTE CLAIM IS RELATIVE TO THREE THINGS, NOT TWO. @3 wrote E-1b as `same closed template + same emitter profile -> same bytes` and the {f0,f1} -> {q0,q1} mutation refutes it directly: the bytes moved on 6 of 9 fixtures and the profile id -- the theorem's entire stated precondition -- stood still. A PROFILE IS CONFIGURATION AND CONFIGURATION DOES NOT BIND AN IMPLEMENTATION THAT DECLINES TO READ IT. So E-1b is scoped to `same closed template + same emitter PROFILE + same emitter ARTIFACT -> same exact bytes`, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_ARTIFACT_ID, which hashes the source text of every function that produces bytes. IT IS PROVENANCE AND IT IS ALLOWED TO OVERMOVE: a comment inside emit() moves it, which would be B1.1's defect in a semantic id and is exactly right for an artifact identity whose claim is `these exact implementation bytes`. AND THE ARTIFACT IDENTITY IS THE WHOLE BYTE-PRODUCING DEPENDENCY CLOSURE, NOT THE OBVIOUS FUNCTIONS. @4 bundled emit, church and the add combinator and missed a module-level enum table emit() reads; one boolean flipped in that table, profile untouched, moved the emitted bytes on 5 of 9 fixtures while the closed template, the profile id and the artifact id all stood still. THE RULE: IF CHANGING A PIECE OF IMPLEMENTATION CAN CHANGE EMITTED BYTES WHILE THE TEMPLATE AND PROFILE STAY FIXED, THAT PIECE BELONGS TO THE ARTIFACT IDENTITY. Repairing the one table would satisfy the falsifier and leave the NEXT helper exactly as exposed, so MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED RATHER THAN MAINTAINED: the battery reads the module's source, derives its module-level bindings, and requires every one a bundled member references to be bundled, to be the profile, or to be DECLARED byte-inert with a reason. A hand-kept bundle is what artifact_versions was when three of its six entries had no reader -- correct the day it was written and silently short afterwards. THREE KINDS OF IDENTITY, AND CONFLATING ANY TWO IS A DEFECT THIS LINE HAS NOW PAID FOR SEPARATELY: semantic relation identity (moves only when meaning moves), serializer CONFIGURATION identity (moves when a knob moves, never for a reword), serializer IMPLEMENTATION identity (moves for any edit to the code). E-1a is unchanged and still says nothing about bytes. B6 framed this as a PAIR -- canonical determinism against semantic equivalence -- which is right at the top and hides that target_term_sem_id sits BETWEEN bytes and meaning rather than at either end. AND THE TWO ADVERSARIES ARE DIFFERENT ANIMALS, which B6 fused. CANONICAL DRIFT (E-F1): same closed template, same relation id, a changed claim about the target term, therefore REFUSE -- it needs NO semantic equivalence and therefore applies to every fixture. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE (E-8): different target_term_sem_id, SAME meaning -- it requires a real equivalence and is applicable only where the fragment supplies one. Fused, the canonical-drift falsifier would lose its adversary the moment a non-commutative operator arrived, for a reason having nothing to do with what it proves. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. AND AT B6.3.1 THAT CAVEAT IS RETIRED RATHER THAN CARRIED, BEFORE THE OPERATOR THAT WOULD HAVE TRIGGERED IT EXISTS. E-8's theorem is that target_term_sem_id identifies THIS EMITTER'S OUTPUT rather than the term's MEANING; it requires a MEANING-PRESERVING STRUCTURAL ALTERNATE and does NOT require an algebraic law of any source operator. A beta redex around the whole term, T -> (lambda z. z T), supplies one generically: measured DIFFERENT target_term_sem_id on 9/9 and SAME decoded outcome on 9/9, against the operand swap's 6/9 applicability. It is independent of the fragment's algebra, reaches the const and input fixtures the swap could never reach, and survives sub and mul by construction. THE BINDER IS CHOSEN AGAINST THE PROFILE rather than hard-coded, because binder_names is a knob and a wrapper spelled z would capture under a profile that named a binder z -- an adversary that silently stops being alpha-safe when a knob moves is the same species as an instrument that stops measuring while still reporting. The operand swap is KEPT as E-8b, an add-specific algebraic measurement whose applicability count is worth watching: when sub arrives it stops being an equivalence and becomes a falsifier for the OPPOSITE property, that operand order IS semantic. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it. AND THE PROJECTION NOW MATCHES THE ONTOLOGY, WHICH AT @2 IT DID NOT. B6.1 ruled label spelling nonsemantic in prose while EMISSION_SEM_ID went on hashing the allocation policy, and the resulting defect was INVERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: editing the PROSE describing the counter moved EMISSION_SEM_ID while bytes and target terms were untouched, and editing the ACTUAL counter inside emit() changed the bytes on 7 of 9 fixtures while EMISSION_SEM_ID stood still. The id was bound to a DESCRIPTION of the policy rather than to the policy -- B1.1's finding that governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when reworded, recurring in the one field B6.1 had corrected the wording of without moving. THE SPLIT: the SEMANTIC target-term encoding commits to Church and add structure, to DUP label EQUALITY AND FRESHNESS relationships, to the alpha and label-permutation quotient, and to the semantic refusals. The CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE commits to counter start, allocation traversal, binder spelling and exact representative bytes, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID, which NO semantic identity cites. THE PROFILE IS INTERPRETED AND NOT DESCRIBED: emit() reads label_counter_start from it, exactly as lower() reads op_lowering_rules since B2.1, so the policy cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving the profile id. AND AT B6.2 THAT WAS TRUE OF ONE FIELD OUT OF SIX, WHICH IS THE DEFECT RECURRING INSIDE ITS OWN FIX. The profile shipped one interpreted knob beside five English sentences and hashed all six. Rewording binder_spelling moved the profile id while bytes, target terms and all eleven cases were untouched; changing the ACTUAL binder spelling from {f0,f1} to {q0,q1} moved the bytes on 6 of 9 fixtures while the profile id stood still; and `label_order` -- `depth-first, operands in declared field order` -- is true of TWO allocation orders that emit different bytes on 5 of 9, so the sentence did not even DETERMINE what it was hashed to identify. THE RULE B6.3 APPLIES: A HASHED FIELD IS A VALUE THE CODE READS OR IT IS NOT HASHED. label_counter_start, label_alloc_order (a closed enum, unknown values a NAMED refusal) and binder_names (the actual names, not a description of how they are chosen) are read by emit(); no hashed value contains a space, so prose has no field it could occupy, which is the structural form TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING.no_names_no_labels uses rather than a promise to keep sentences out. The prose is intact and unhashed in CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_NOTES. An English sentence beside a hard-coded constant is two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed, which is precisely how the field came to be false in both directions. AND NO ALLOCATION POLICY IS HASHED UPSTREAM EITHER: TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING named a counter start, so changing an emitter's allocation re-cut the TEMPLATE, LOWERING and INSTANTIATION identities -- a layer whose whole claim is that no allocation exists in it cannot also commit to how one is performed two layers down. THE RECEIPT IS UNCHANGED AND STAYS THAT WAY: no byte digest is added. Exact bytes are PROVENANCE and belong beside executable_artifact_id. AND AT B7 THE FRAGMENT WIDENS, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME THIS RELATION HAS HAD TO SAY WHAT IT CANNOT DO. `sub` is the first construct whose SOURCE meaning does not fit in the TARGET: the frozen core's `sub` is true subtraction and evaluates sub(2,3) to -1, while the executable encoding represents NON-NEGATIVE Church naturals and has no image for -1. THE SOURCE LANGUAGE THEREFORE PROPERLY CONTAINS THE REPRESENTABLE TARGET FRAGMENT, which is what a partial compiler is, and emission refuses by name -- emit-sub-underflow -- against its own CODOMAIN. THREE OTHER PLACES TO PUT THAT REFUSAL WERE CONSIDERED AND ARE WRONG. SATURATION is a miscompilation and not a design choice: raw Church subtraction ((n PRED) m) normalises to 0 whenever n >= m, so compiling the core's sub onto it answers 0 where the source says -1 -- and the damage is not confined to the root, because (2-3)+2 then decodes to 2 against the source's 1, an answer that is itself perfectly representable and therefore invisible to any check on the RESULT. A LOWERING PRECONDITION cannot be written at all: sub(input x, input y) has no underflow fact until an invocation binds the ports, so one template emits under {x:5,y:2} and refuses under {x:2,y:5}, and at lowering they are the same object. A SOURCE REFUSAL would change the language to suit the compiler and move CORE_SEM_ID, re-identifying every program ever written. AND THIS IS NOT SOURCE-REFUSAL TO TARGET-REFUSAL PRESERVATION AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS PROGRESS ON IT: for sub(2,3) the source DOES NOT REFUSE, it evaluates to -1 correctly, and the compiler declines. No target term is produced, so no target outcome exists and none is claimed; the evidence says so rather than leaving the absence to be read as a gap. THE DECISION IS TAKEN BEFORE ANY KNOB IS READ. Whether a closed template has an image is a property of the template and the codomain, not a serialization choice, so representability is checked before the profile is validated and no profile -- including two deliberately broken ones -- can turn a domain refusal into an acceptance or into a different refusal. AND EMISSION EMITS SUBTRACTION RATHER THAN COMPUTING IT. The representability walk evaluates the closed template under the source arithmetic and computes exactly the value a constant folder would return, then DISCARDS it: every emitting sub fixture carries real PRED structure, is longer than emit(church(itsOwnValue)) would be, and is reduced by the runtime under its own interaction-net dynamics -- 96 frames over APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM and DUP-SUP= for sub(5,2), where a folded numeral would reduce in zero. Folding would make the integration theorem a theorem about the compiler's own walk. AND THE OPERAND SWAP HAS CHANGED SIDES EXACTLY AS @5 PREDICTED. E-8b was meaning-preserving only because addition commutes; for sub it is a FALSIFIER for the opposite property, that operand order IS semantic -- E-10 sub(5,2) emits and E-17 sub(2,5) is refused over the same two operands with the fields exchanged. Its applicable set EXCLUDES BY NAME any fixture whose two operands are byte-equal, because sub(2,2) is its own swap and a symmetric pair cannot reveal order-sensitivity -- INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c's own species, and the first draft of the case included them and failed.

entries.statement: A BOUNDED CLAIM IS A CLAIM ABOUT A DOMAIN, AND ITS EVIDENCE MUST BE CHECKABLE BY SOMETHING THAT TRUSTS NEITHER THE CLAIM NOR THE THING THAT PRODUCED IT. A BoundedProofBundle states a proposition, the finite variable domains it is claimed over, and one CaseEvidence per assignment carrying both sides' full compiler chain -- program identity, lowering receipt, instantiation receipt, emission receipt, native semantic film, target normal-form identity and decoded outcome -- plus an aggregate. THE VERDICT FIELD IS THE ONE THING A CHECKER MAY NEVER READ AS TRUE. An aggregate that certifies itself is derivation.instantiation-identity@1's defect at the END of the chain instead of the start: the object that produced the evidence would also be the thing saying the evidence is sufficient. The checker COMPUTES a verdict from its own refusals and compares the bundle's to it. THE DOMAIN IS DERIVED BY THE CHECKER, NOT READ FROM THE BUNDLE'S COUNT. Coverage is the Cartesian product the checker computes itself, by a DIFFERENT algorithm from the generator's -- mixed-radix index arithmetic against iterative expansion -- and matched as a SET. Importing the generator's enumeration would make 'the cases cover the domain' a tautology about one function agreeing with itself, which is the same shape as an emitter canonicalising its own output. A TOTAL IS NOT A COVERAGE. Sixty-four cases over sixty-three unique assignments is the exact shape a complete-looking bundle takes when it is short, and it survives every hash if the aggregate is resealed around the duplicate. Completed, distinct, missing and failed are recomputed and cross-checked by arithmetic; the case-set commitment is over the SORTED, UNDEDUPLICATED assignment ids so a repeat does not hash like a distinct member. THE DOMAIN MAY NOT WIDEN AFTER THE EVIDENCE IS CUT, and there are two forms. The lazy form leaves domain_sem_id behind and is caught by recomputing it. The COHERENT form moves the domain, its id and the expected count together, so every hash agrees and the bundle is a well-formed statement about eighty assignments carrying evidence for sixty-four -- and only the derived coverage refuses it. That is why the product is derived rather than compared. A THEOREM ABOUT TWO PROGRAMS MUST CHECK THAT THERE ARE TWO. If both sides of a case reach the same target_term_sem_id the case asserts that a program equals itself, and sixty-four of those still aggregate to VERIFIED. The two sides are required to DIFFER in target term and AGREE in decoded outcome, with the source evaluator agreeing independently as a third opinion that is not the referee. THE FILM IS THE ONE PART A CHECKER CANNOT RE-DERIVE, because it is a native execution, so it is REPLAYED -- on TWO RUNTIME CLASSES, one of them an allocator whose heap ids are non-monotone. That is where state.exec-identity@1's separation of execution identity from semantic identity is cashed rather than asserted: a readback inferring dependency order from an id integer fails here, in the artifact whose correctness depends on it, rather than silently years later. AND THE BOUND IS PART OF THE ARTIFACT, NOT PART OF A LEDGER SENTENCE. Sixty-four assignments verified exhaustively is not distributivity over the naturals; it is not an induction and nothing in it generalises past 3. A bundle whose scope record does not say so is making a different and larger claim, and the scope travels with the evidence because the evidence travels.
entries.evidence: proof_bundle.mjs / proof_check.mjs / proof_forgeries.mjs, gate `gov-proof`. x * (y + z) = (x * y) + (x * z) over {0,1,2,3}^3: 64 cases, 128 program sides, 128 native films. The checker DERIVES 64 assignments from the declared domains and matches them as a set -- 64 distinct, 0 missing, 0 duplicated, 0 outside the domain -- then re-derives all 128 chains from the proposition IN THE BUNDLE and reproduces every lowering, instantiation and emission receipt field for field, replays all 128 films on FloatRt and ScrambledFloatRt, and re-decodes all 128 outcomes from normal forms it reached itself. 64/64 cases reach DIFFERENT target terms and agree on the decoded outcome; 7 of them normalise past the SEMSTATE-CANONICAL-v1 signature-compaction bound, so the decoder retired at B8.1 could not have read their answers -- the widening is load-bearing for this artifact rather than done in advance. NON-VACUITY IS ITS OWN GATE: proof_forgeries.mjs mutates the bundle in memory 13 ways and requires each to draw ITS OWN refusal code, digesting before and after so a forgery that forged nothing FAILS rather than counting. The two that matter most are the aggregate RESEALED around its own duplicate -- internally consistent at every hash, refused by arithmetic -- and the domain widened WITH its id and expected count updated, which no hash check can see and the derived coverage refuses. Three further forgeries live in the negative battery against the checker's INDEPENDENCE, because those are invisible in a passing run: the checker importing the generator's enumeration, the checker reading the verdict instead of computing one, and the bounded scope leaving the artifact.

entries.statement: AUTHENTICATION IS NOT VERIFICATION. A field being inside a hash is meaningless unless the verifier DERIVES it, CHECKS it, or explicitly classifies it as NON-SEMANTIC. For every machine-semantic record accepted under a proof protocol the checker owns the EXACT set and interpretation of accepted fields; an unknown semantic field is a REFUSAL, and extending the vocabulary is a protocol revision rather than an addition to a record. THIS IS emission.profile-is-interpreted@1's RULE ONE LAYER OUT: that law says a hashed field is a value the code READS, and read it as a rule about PROSE -- it is a rule about VOCABULARY, because a producer who can ADD a field can state things the checker never agreed to without altering any value the checker looks at. P1, P2 and P3 each shipped accepting a resealed scope.proves_all_naturals / proves_all_integers / transitive, and P3's claim and operand records had no vocabulary at all, so the field did not even have to be resealed. NON-AUTHORITATIVE PROSE LIVES IN A SEPARATE TRUST DOMAIN, never nested inside an authenticated record: an unhashed seat inside a semantic object is where evidence hides, and bounding such a seat guards a hole rather than filling it. A CHECKER MAY NOT LET A PRODUCER NAME WHAT A PASS PROVED -- canonical descriptions are RENDERED by the checker from the artifact it actually checked. AND THE PUBLIC RESULT IS COHERENT: ok is true exactly when the verdict is VERIFIED, so a parent asking `verdict` and a parent asking `ok` cannot disagree about the same child.
entries.evidence: schema.mjs (grammar + publicResult) with the key sets declared inside proof_check.mjs, domain_check.mjs and compose_check.mjs and NOT imported, gate `gov-proof`. Fifteen record types gated: bundle, claim, scope, proposition/program, refusal contract, refusal, refusal_witness, evidence, case, side, equality, execution_provenance, operand, child, aggregate. Codes proof-/domain-/compose-vocabulary-unknown. REPRODUCED BEFORE REPAIR: 8 of 8 forged artifacts accepted by the shipped P3 pack, including a certificate printing THE RIEMANN HYPOTHESIS IS PROVED FOR ALL NON-TRIVIAL ZEROES under DOMAIN-CHECK: PASS, and P1 printing P = NP under PROOF-CHECK: PASS after one further reseal. 12 aggregate fields were hashed and compared to nothing -- including P1's `failed`, the headline count of failed cases -- and all 12 are derived now. All three checkers could answer {ok:false, verdict:VERIFIED}. AFTER: 0 of 8 accepted. Forgeries proof 24/24, domain 28/28, compose 20/20; negative battery 377/377 including grammar-accepts-unknown-keys and public-result-incoherent, both verified to parse, load and flip exactly their named property. grid_check probes grammar() and publicResult() directly and feeds checkBundle a bundle that FAILS WHILE ASSERTING VERIFIED, which discriminates a checker that reads its verdict from one that computes it.

entries.statement: IDENTITY, AVAILABILITY and WARRANT are three things, and a content address supplies the first two only. A content hash says WHICH artifact is meant; a store says WHERE its bytes are; that it was ACCEPTED is neither, and may be established only by running the checker of the artifact's own protocol -- on every citation, including one whose bytes this run has already accepted. A RESOLVING VERIFIER MUST RE-DERIVE THE ADDRESS FROM THE BYTES IT RECEIVED, and over the PARSED OBJECT rather than the received octets, so that what it authenticated and what it reasons about cannot be two different values. The store is untrusted by construction; the standing counter-example is an INPUT-addressed action cache, whose key cannot validate its value, so a client must simply trust whoever wrote it. AND A CACHED VERDICT IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE BYTES: it is a property of the bytes AND the checker AND its version, so issuing one is a verifier-owned authority decision and never a hash. Until such an authority exists the same artifact cited twice is CHECKED TWICE, and the gap between child_checker_invocations and unique_subtree_roots is the MEASURED price of not having issued a warrant rather than a cost avoided in silence. THERE IS A FOURTH THING AND IT COMES BEFORE THE OTHER THREE: CITABILITY. An artifact must carry the fields its citation identity binds, and measured against the shipped P3 artifact verifiedClaimSemId THREW `certificate-incomplete: chain_ids` -- so a composed certificate could not be NAMED at all, and P3's declared non-transitivity was a hole rather than a policy. A composition's chain is DERIVED from the children it resolved and may never be declared, which is law:proof.claimant-may-not-define-the-semantics one layer out. RECURSION TERMINATES BY A DECLARED DEPTH CEILING AND NOT BY AN APPEAL TO PREIMAGE RESISTANCE: a cycle cannot be sealed, measured over 512 attempted fixpoints with no convergence, so the cycle guard is declared DEFENCE IN DEPTH and not load-bearing -- but a long CHAIN is not a cycle, is perfectly constructible, and is refused at the shipped bound by a real witness rather than by a grep of the constant.
entries.evidence: cas.mjs (artifactRoot over the parsed object; resolveArtifact re-deriving the root and naming all four outcomes), nest_bundle.mjs, nest_check.mjs -- whose child table, connectives, scope, grammar and chain derivation are each declared inside it and NOT imported, for the fifth round running -- and nest_forgeries.mjs; gate `gov-nest`. THE SHIPPED DAG is D = C2 AND C1, C2 = C1 AND A, C1 = A AND B: a diamond twice over, whose shared node is deliberately the 1.3 MB P1 bundle because a diamond over a cheap node measures nothing. A 4,518-byte artifact names 3,620,908 bytes of proof: 8 citations over 4 distinct artifacts, 1,266,802 bytes stored once (2.86x), 8 child-checker invocations of which 4 re-verify bytes already accepted, depth 3, and 404 films replayed TRANSITIVELY against 0 replayed by the parent -- structural, because nest_check.mjs directly imports no kernel, no emitter, no decoder and not the derivation protocol's encoder either. nest_forgeries.mjs 26/26 across 14 refusal codes. The headline forgery is an artifact with nothing wrong with it: every root re-derives, every certificate recomputes, every aggregate reseals, every address resolves -- over a child its own checker refuses. Grid probes are behavioural and synthesise their own store; disabling the root re-derivation in cas.mjs flips exactly one of the five reported booleans.

entries.statement: A CONTENT ADDRESS NAMES BYTES OR IT NAMES NOTHING. Hashing the PARSED object rather than the received octets makes a root a description of a parse result: any byte string that parses to that object resolves under it, so pretty and compact encodings share an address -- and a DUPLICATE OBJECT MEMBER NAME, which JSON.parse silently resolves in favour of the last occurrence, lets bytes saying one thing be AUTHENTICATED as an artifact saying another. That is a CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION hazard rather than a formatting preference: RFC 8259 calls parser behaviour on duplicate names unpredictable, I-JSON forbids them, RFC 8785 requires I-JSON, and an implementation keeping the FIRST duplicate would verify a different object under the same root while believing it had checked the same artifact. THE RULE: a resolver must require received_bytes === canonical_encoding(parsed_object) before it hashes anything, and the store must hold canonical bytes. Duplicate names, key reordering, alternate number spellings and whitespace are then all refused by ONE equality rather than by a special case each, and duplicate-key rejection is a CONSEQUENCE rather than a check -- canonical output emits every key once, so bytes containing a repeat can never equal the canonical form of what they parse to. THE ROOT IS TAKEN OVER THE PARSED OBJECT AND THE WIRE IS REQUIRED TO EQUAL IT, which is not the same as hashing the octets: what is authenticated and what is reasoned about must be one value. Human-readable encodings remain an export and presentation format. AND THE ENCODER MUST BE MEASURED AGAINST THE STANDARD RATHER THAN INSPECTED -- an encoder that sorted by CODE POINT instead of UTF-16 CODE UNIT passes every vector that contains no surrogate pair.
entries.evidence: cas.mjs v0.2.0 (canonicalWire IS canonicalBytes, so the tree has ONE canonical encoder rather than two things called canonical that nothing compares; resolveArtifact requires the equality and names seven outcomes). jcs_vectors.mjs, gate `gov-nest`: 3/3 against published RFC 8785 data -- the RFC's own section 3.2.2/3.2.3 worked example, the reference suite's french.json, and a UTF-16 code-unit ordering vector in which U+1F602 (surrogate pair, first unit D83D) must precede U+FB33 and a code-point implementation puts it last. THREE VECTORS ARE NOT THE REFERENCE SUITE and full conformance is NOT claimed. Reproduced against the shipped P4 pack before repair: the same object indented resolved under one root (4880 vs 4509 bytes, resolveArtifact ok on both), and {"protocol":"TRVM-EVIL-v1", ... ,"protocol":"TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v1"} verified at ok:true with zero refusals.

entries.statement: A LOCATOR MAY RENAME THE ARTIFACT CARRYING A PROOF. IT MAY NOT RENAME THE PROOF. A transport or version identifier used to ACQUIRE evidence may affect the identity of the containing artifact, and may not alter the semantic identity of the claim that evidence establishes. P4 placed artifact_root inside claim.operands and therefore inside nested_claim_sem_id, so rewording one English annotation on a leaf -- non-semantic by construction, and measured to leave that leaf's verified_claim_sem_id untouched -- MOVED every ancestor's claim id, aggregate id and certificate id. The planes are separate records with separate identities: CLAIM says what is asserted, REFERENCES say where the bytes are, EVIDENCE says what holds, STRUCTURE says what shape the DAG is, and VERIFIER EXECUTION is not in the artifact at all. AND OPERATIONAL COUNTS ARE NOT PROOF SEMANTICS: how many times a checker was invoked, and whether it reused a derivation, are facts about a verification run that no artifact can be right about; putting them in the claim or the aggregate means a sound verifier changing STRATEGY renames the theorem. What an artifact may state about its own shape must be strategy-independent -- edge counts, distinct-artifact counts and byte totals are, `checker_evaluations` is not. THE SEPARATION CREATES THE ONE THING SEPARATION ALWAYS CREATES, a way for the halves to disagree, so operands and references must be matched as SETS and every citation recomputed from what was RESOLVED.
entries.evidence: nest_bundle.mjs / nest_check.mjs v0.2.0, protocol TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v2 (a record-shape change is a protocol revision, per law:proof.semantic-vocabulary-closed@1). Gate `gov-nest`. MEASURED POSITIVELY rather than by refusing a negation: rewording one annotation on the P1 leaf holds 10 semantic names -- every claim id, aggregate id and certificate id at all three composition levels -- and moves 4 addresses, and the rebuilt DAG verifies. Against P4 the same edit moved all three claim ids. The grid enforces the boundary where it is enforceable: an operand carrying an artifact_root is refused nest-vocabulary-unknown, and the claim id still moves when the certificate does.

entries.statement: A CALLER MAY TIGHTEN A VERIFIER'S RESOURCE POLICY AND MAY NOT WEAKEN IT while still claiming that verifier's verdict. P4 declared a shipped depth ceiling of 32, wrote that a test may lower it and never raise it, and exposed it as an ordinary argument: checkNestBundle(chain40, {store}) REFUSED and checkNestBundle(chain40, {store, max_depth: 1000}) returned VERIFIED over a 40-deep chain, with the artifact's own positive witness for the guard defeated by a number. Five rounds had by then established that the checker owns its scope, its absence vocabulary, its citation semantics and its grammar; the API caller still owned the acceptance policy. A weakening request is a NAMED REFUSAL, not a silent clamp, and the EFFECTIVE policy carries an identity reported beside the verdict so a reader can tell which policy accepted an artifact. AND AN UNTRUSTED STORE MAKES THE MISSING BOUNDS URGENT: it supplies not only wrong artifacts but arbitrarily deep, wide and large ones, so artifact bytes, total resolved bytes, operands per node and distinct-artifact count are all bounds something hostile would otherwise choose. A CEILING ON CITATION CHAINS IS ABOUT THE DAG'S HEIGHT, NOT THE RECURSION'S DEPTH -- a resolver that only descends into COMPOSED artifacts reaches a smaller number than the longest path, so checking depth-of-recursion accepts a DAG taller than the stated bound.
entries.evidence: nest_check.mjs v0.2.0: SHIPPED_POLICY with six fields, effectivePolicy() comparing each against it, refusal nest-policy-weakened, policyId reported in measured. Gate `gov-nest`. Measured: a genuine 40-deep chain is refused at the shipped ceiling of 32; max_depth:1000 is refused rather than obeyed; max_depth:2 still refuses the honest height-3 DAG, so tightening works. derivation_reuse:false counts as a tightening because it does more work. The height-versus-depth error was found by that same tightening test -- max_depth:2 accepted a height-3 DAG because the resolver's recursion reached only 2.

entries.statement: A VERIFIER COMPUTES A VERDICT FROM ONE IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT IT OWNS, TAKEN AT INGRESS. After ingress no semantic check, identity computation, policy decision, measurement or diagnostic may reread caller-owned state. A checker handed a live host-language OBJECT is handed something the caller can still change, and one getter is enough: measured against the shipped P4.1 pack on TWO protocols at once, `references.contract.address_is_a_warrant` returned false to the first read and true to every later one while checkNestBundle returned VERIFIED and the same object then serialised with address_is_a_warrant true; and `claim.scope.generalizes_beyond_domain` returned false for the three reads P1's checker makes and true afterwards, with checkBundle returning VERIFIED over what then read as an UNBOUNDED scope. THIS IS THE MUTABLE-INPUT RULE THE WORLD/AUTHORITY LADDER ALREADY REACHED, rediscovered independently by the proof subsystem: do not authenticate one read of caller-owned data and continue reasoning from later reads of it. P4.1 already snapshotted everything it fetched from an untrusted store and then stopped touching the store; the ROOT input had no equivalent transition, so the one artifact a verifier is handed directly was the one artifact it did not own. THE PREFERRED PUBLIC BOUNDARY IS BYTES -- check*Bytes(rawBytes) -> strict canonical ingress -> owned plain data -> checker -- because bytes cannot have a getter. An object convenience API is legitimate provided it canonicalises ONCE and then uses only the owned snapshot; the one read taken at ingress is the read the verdict is about.
entries.evidence: schema.mjs `ownSnapshot` (canonicalise once, re-parse into plain data), applied as an ingress wrapper to ALL FOUR protocols -- proof_check.mjs, domain_check.mjs, compose_check.mjs and nest_check.mjs -- with named `*-ingress-refused` codes rather than an escaping exception. nest_check.mjs additionally exposes `checkNestBytes`. Gate `gov-nest`, and grid probe `input-read-once`: a live getter is read EXACTLY ONCE by each checker, measured on P4 and P1 together, and a getter returning the hostile value AT INGRESS is refused so the single read is load-bearing rather than lucky.

entries.statement: AN IMPLEMENTATION UNDER CONFORMANCE TEST MAY NOT GENERATE, REWRITE OR REDEFINE THE EXPECTED VALUES AGAINST WHICH THAT SAME IMPLEMENTATION IS JUDGED. A generator that imports the live implementation and writes its results into the normative vector tree, run by the verification script, computes both the answer and the answer key: measured, changing one implementation-only constant -- the artifact-root domain separator, from TRVM-ARTIFACT-ROOT-v2 to -v999 -- while touching no specification moved every expected root and the conformance gate reported PASS. The corpus MUST be committed, MUST carry a spec revision, and MUST be READ by a verification run; regenerating it is a normative act that names the revision it produces and that no gate performs. A verification run MUST leave the specification tree byte-identical, and that MUST be measured rather than promised. AND AN EXPECTATION IS COMPARED FOR EXACT EQUALITY, NOT CONTAINMENT: a declared refusal SET checked as a subset of the measured one lets a checker acquire additional refusal semantics silently -- a single-fault vector given a second fault still passed. Sets are sorted before they are frozen, so byte equality IS set equality and refusal ORDER remains outside the protocol. THE SAME CIRCULARITY EXISTS ONE LEVEL UP: an audit whose denominator is the checker's OWN grammar cannot see a field deleted from the checker, from the check that enforced it and from the producer -- measured, the audit reports 45/45 PASS while the protocol has 46 fields. A normative machine-readable grammar is required, and THE RUNTIME MUST NOT IMPORT IT, because two declarations that read one object agree by construction.
entries.evidence: spec_vectors.mjs v0.2.0: VERIFY mode builds a candidate corpus in memory, compares it byte for byte with the frozen corpus at docs/spec/proof-wire/vectors/, names which expectation moved, and digests the specification tree before and after to prove it wrote nothing; UPDATE mode requires --spec-revision and is run by a human. spec_agreement.mjs compares the normative schema at docs/spec/proof-wire/schema/ with the checker's own exported declarations -- 10 record grammars, 46 fields and planes, 28 refusal codes, scope, reference contract, child-protocol table, both domain-separation strings and 6 policy values -- and asserts on the SOURCE of all five runtime files that none of them references the schema. Gate `gov-nest`; grid booleans conformance-oracle-frozen and spec-grammar-agrees, each falsified independently.

entries.statement: AN UNTRUSTED WIRE BOUNDARY BOUNDS THE OCTETS THAT ARRIVED, BEFORE ANYTHING LOOKS AT THEM. The ingress order is: confirm the input is byte-like; COPY it into storage the verifier owns; apply the byte-length bound; decode UTF-8 fatally; parse strictly; canonicalise and require octet equality; only then verify semantics. Bounding a CANONICAL size instead is bounding a number you can only learn by decoding, parsing and re-encoding the thing you were trying not to spend that much work on -- measured, an oversized buffer of invalid UTF-8 reported an ingress refusal rather than a budget refusal, because the decode ran first. AND OWNERSHIP MEANS A COPY. Retaining a caller's buffer, or a buffer an untrusted store handed back, leaves the verifier reasoning about storage somebody else can still write to; law:proof.verifier-input-owned@1 is only literally true when the octets are copied at ingress.
