derivation_language.decided: before the expressiveness round, not during it — the same discipline as film_identity_forward_declaration
derivation_language.ruling: SMALL TOTAL CORE plus NAMED SEMANTIC PRIMITIVES. The core stays small and total. Complex behaviour arrives as {op:'prim', primitive_sem_id, args}, never as if/while/function/closure/recursion/eval. The reason is the one this whole line of work has been establishing: a general programming language at the derivation boundary re-admits the unbounded capability container that law:derivation.environment-confinement@1 was falsified by, in a form that serializes.
derivation_language.primitive_identity: primitive_sem_id must be content-bound, not a name. H(primitive language/version + canonical input/output contract + semantic specification identity + conformance-vector identity). 'componentReachability' as a bare string would be exactly the caller-selected label the program_sem_id design refuses. program_sem_id contains primitive_sem_id; each implementation of the primitive carries refinement evidence beneath it.
derivation_language.first_primitive: component reachability, and it is chosen because it is materially harder than arithmetic: graph traversal, data-dependent reads, support, adjacency footprints and the phantom-scope case all appear in it at once. It also has a total semantic definition over a finite canonical grant snapshot — general recursion is not required to express it, which is the property that keeps the core total.
derivation_language.data_dependent_reads: traversal discovers what to read as it goes (read adj:a -> discover b -> read edge:a|b -> ...), which is precisely why the grant may be broader than the footprint. Under the snapshot model the authority hands over a bounded world slice and the evaluator logs the subset consumed. This is the concrete case law:derivation.grant-footprint-separation@1 exists for.
derivation_language.not_built: no prim op exists. The core is frozen; the primitive CATALOG is not, and a prim extension bumps the core version and therefore every program id, deliberately.
derivation_language.frozen: TRVM-DERIVE-CORE-v1 is FROZEN as of round 16 — grammar, value domain, arithmetic, signed zero, evaluation order, footprint-as-set, totality and refusal vocabulary — with a content-bound core_sem_id load-bearing inside every program_sem_id. See law:derivation.core-semantics@1.

target_encoding.name: TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1
target_encoding.what: a canonical encoding of the TARGET TERM, before heap allocation — a different object from the runtime heap state that SEMSTATE-CANONICAL-v1 identifies.
target_encoding.why: it resolves an ordering inversion. 'The same AST lowers to byte-identical target syntax' needs a target NOTATION to be byte-identical in; if that notation were the runtime-state canonicaliser, the spike would depend on the very C work the film round is supposed to deliver. Term identity and runtime-state identity are separate, so the spike does not wait for the film.
target_encoding.caveat: ic32's existing textual syntax may serve IF it has a proven unique parse/format round trip and canonical variable naming. If not, do not bless pretty-printed text — use a small canonical target AST / prefix serialization.

three_properties: the same Derive AST lowers to byte-identical target-term bytes
JS evaluate(source) and ic32(normalize(target)) decode to the same outcome
the resulting ic32 execution emits and replays an ordinary TRVM transition film

identities.chain: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id + inputs_sem_id)-> closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id -(native film)-> target_nf_sem_id -(decode_sem_id)-> outcome_sem_id
identities.chain_is_derived: THE NODE SEQUENCE IN THE TWO CHAIN STRINGS IS CHECKED AGAINST REFINEMENT_CHAIN IN lowering.mjs, IN ORDER, AND NOT TRANSCRIBED. Both strings above stated a chain that stopped being the chain: this one still ran lowering straight to target_term_sem_id, the B1-era shape from before the template layer existed; the inputs_model one below carried the B1.2 shape and missed closed_template_sem_id and emission_sem_id, which B2.1 added when the emission split fired. A prose chain beside a data chain is two artifacts that can disagree while only one is executable — the same species as the law count, the case count and the rung count this tree has already watched drift. grid_check now extracts every *_sem_id token from each string IN ORDER and requires it to equal REFINEMENT_CHAIN's ids, so a node added in code forces the prose and a node dropped from the prose fails the gate.
identities.reference_side: the JS derivation evaluator independently produces outcome_sem_id from program_sem_id + inputs
identities.program_sem_id_is_not_replaced: the lowered term's id must NOT replace program_sem_id. Keeping them distinct is what makes the chain a refinement STATEMENT rather than a renaming.
identities.why_outcome_not_value: REFUSAL IS ALSO SEMANTICS. An outcome is {status:'value', value} or {status:'refused', reason} content-addressed under TRVM-DERIVE-OUTCOME-v1. A value-only identity cannot state that two implementations agreed about program-arith-non-finite, which is exactly the agreement the frozen core exists to make checkable.
identities.outcome_encoding: outcome_sem_id MUST NOT hash a human-readable reason string. Rendering 'program-type: add of non-number' is DIAGNOSTICS; hashing it would recreate round 16's 'the identity bound a spelling' defect one layer up, where semantic identity would depend on English punctuation and two conforming implementations could differ by a comma. TRVM-DERIVE-OUTCOME-v1 encodes an outcome STRUCTURALLY: {status:'value', value} or {status:'refused', code, locus} where `code` is a canonical refusal code from the frozen core's refusal vocabulary and `locus` carries whatever detail is actually semantic (the offending op and path), never a rendered sentence.

lowering_spike.layer_separation: lowering proves source program -> target term; the FILM proves target term -> target normal form transitions; DECODING proves target normal form -> target outcome; the refinement receipt proves source outcome == target outcome. The film must not be asked to prove source-language equivalence — its job is to witness the target machine's execution.
lowering_spike.decision_rule: if the spike is clean, lowering into ic32 is preferred over a second dedicated C interpreter beside it — one execution substrate rather than two. If the mapping is awkward, it is NOT adopted. The point of a spike is that it can fail.
lowering_spike.execution_grade: FILM-EVIDENCED — six chained APP-LAM frames the kernel's own replaySemFilm accepts on two runtime classes, on top of an execution the ObservedExecutionHost drove. Was OBSERVED in round 25.
lowering_spike.film_grade: COVERED for this fixture. Round 25 recorded it OPEN because ic32_film v0.1.0 refused on film-dup-cell-present; measuring the kernel's film for the same term showed the refusal was right about the fixture and wrong about the reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires no dup rule. The precondition moved from PRESENCE to ENABLEDNESS at v0.2.0, and at v0.3.0 it moved again, to the two ERA rules the church_exp_2_2 measurement showed have no witness. THE SIX DUP-* RULES AND THE d:/v: LOCI ARE NO LONGER OPEN — but they were closed by church_exp_2_2 under film.native-emission@2, not by this fixture, which fires none of them and whose six APP-LAM frames are unchanged. AND AT B4 THE ERA RULES CLOSED TOO, again by their own purpose-built minimal fixtures and not by this one, which fires neither. AND AT B5 THE BUDGET TERMINAL CLOSED -- again not by this fixture, which runs to quiescence in six frames and has no partial execution to evidence. STILL OPEN: canonical-locus alias precedence, which is refused rather than resolved; C-side replay; and film-too-many-frames, which no term tried reaches because MAXPATH binds first on every one of them -- the guard itself is witnessed by a limits build.

inputs_model.ruling: TWO LEVELS, TWO IDENTITIES. lowering: program -> parameterized target TEMPLATE, identity a function of the program alone. instantiation: template + inputs -> closed target TERM. 'Parameterized versus instantiated' was a false choice: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed.
inputs_model.chain: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id + inputs_sem_id)-> closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id -(native film)-> target_nf_sem_id -(decode_sem_id)-> outcome_sem_id, with source outcome == target outcome at the last node

THE HOLDOUT COMMITS RECIPES AND MACHINE-EVALUABLE PREDICATES, not English and not final JS artifacts: 10 constructions, 15 recipe steps, 19 predicates over eight frozen operators, 0 recorded hashes. holdout_score.mjs is PREREGISTRATION: reveal verifies the commitment and REFUSES to score a mismatch, an adapter applies committed recipes and emits neutral observations, and the scorer knows eight operators and no TRVM. changelog_from_1_56_0: law:proof.protocol-oracle-is-environment-independent@1 — the frozen oracle was environment-coupled. spec_vectors regenerated its candidate from the LOCAL producer, whose artifacts bind execution_provenance.executable_artifact_id, so a reviewer on another machine saw every semantic id hold, every complete root move, and 17 conformance disagreements. law:proof.spec-release-bound@1 — the normative prose was bound to nothing. REVISION NUMBERS ARE LABELS; DIGESTS ARE IDENTITIES. protocol_version, spec_revision and public_corpus_revision move independently, and a conformance report cites the digest because two releases can both call themselves revision 1.

Ten constructions with SPEC-DERIVED expectations and ZERO recorded hashes, outside the spec tree so shipping the specification cannot leak them; only the commitment travels. THE VECTOR TREE HAS THREE STATES NOW: vectors/public/ (green conformance), the committed holdout (hidden), and requirements/open/ (declared-open). Full RFC 8785 conformance is a DECLARED-OPEN requirement with weird.json and unicode.json named as absent and why — a red mandatory vector is not a passing gate with an asterisk.

THE KEY-ORDER DEFECT FAMILY APPEARED A THIRD TIME, in the spec-vector DIAGNOSTIC comparator, and a FOURTH time in live_dag.mjs on its first run — in the same round that fixed it. It cannot create a false PASS (the outer comparison is canonical) but it invented disagreement rows, which is the verdict/diagnosis distinction failing on the diagnosis side.
changelog_from_1_55_0: law:proof.conformance-oracle-frozen@1 — the implementation was computing its own answer key. spec_vectors.mjs imported the live code and WROTE the expected values into the normative vector tree, and verify.sh ran it: changing ARTIFACT_ROOT_PROTOCOL to -v999 while touching no specification moved every expected root and the gate said PASS. REFUSAL EXPECTATIONS ARE COMPARED FOR EXACT SET EQUALITY, not containment. A single-fault vector given a second fault kept passing while its measured set grew.

spec_agreement.mjs — the gate field_audit.mjs cannot be. law:proof.byte-budget-before-parse@1 — the ceiling was applied to a CANONICAL size, which is a number you only learn by doing the work the ceiling exists to prevent. Oversized invalid UTF-8 reported an ingress refusal instead of a budget refusal. And every buffer is COPIED at ingress, from the caller and from the store.

THE SPECIFICATION GAINED WHAT A BLIND IMPLEMENTER NEEDS: TRVM-VERIFIED-CLAIM-v1.md (the certificate preimage, the per-protocol claim member, and why leaf_chains is awkward and deliberately unrepaired), the verifier-policy identity formula, the aggregate and structure derivations, and complete canonical CAS fixture octets in the vector tree.

REFUSAL OUTCOMES ARE NORMALISED ACROSS PARSER STRICTNESS. A strict reader that rejects a duplicate member name or invalid UTF-8 in the parser MUST report non-canonical-wire and invalid-utf8 respectively, not malformed. The internal detection stage is not protocol semantics — which matters because Go's json/v2 rejects both by default where Node does not.

The upstream RFC 8785 corpus is a GATE now, read as FILES from docs/spec/proof-wire/vectors/jcs-upstream/ — a PARTIAL import whose PROVENANCE.md records what is absent and why. Full conformance is still not claimed.
changelog_from_1_54_0: law:proof.verifier-input-owned@1 — a getter was enough to defeat two protocols at once. address_is_a_warrant read false to P4.1's one read and true to everyone afterwards (VERIFIED); generalizes_beyond_domain read false for P1's three reads and true afterwards (VERIFIED). aggregate.nested_verdict WAS HASHED AND UNREAD — B6.3 for the thirteenth time, in a protocol written two rounds after the law that forbids it. Set to REFUSED and resealed, P4.1 answered VERIFIED over an artifact that said of itself it was refused.

field_audit.mjs IS THE SWEEP THAT ENDS THAT SPECIES. The denominator is the checker's OWN grammar; every field of every record is classified DERIVED / CHECKED / NON_SEMANTIC with no fourth category and no unclassified escape; and each is PERTURBED with the parent's identities resealed — DERIVED and CHECKED must be refused, NON_SEMANTIC must still verify, which is the half that catches over-classification. 46 fields, 31/12/3.

THE WIRE IS UTF-8 BYTES, NOT A DECODED HOST STRING. canonicalWire returned a JS string, directoryStore read with the forgiving `utf8` decoder, and every budget counted String.length — so a raw 0xFF became U+FFFD before the canonical equality ran (two byte strings, one artifact, again) and a 29-byte artifact passed a 16-byte ceiling. Stores return Buffer, the decode is fatal, the comparison is Buffer.compare, and artifactBytes means UTF-8 bytes. No root and no semantic id moved.

canonicalBytes ACCEPTED LONE SURROGATES, in values and in keys, which RFC 8785 says must terminate canonicalisation with an error. Nothing in the tree contains one, so no identity moved; what changed is that one cannot be introduced.

THE ROOT ARTIFACT WAS EXEMPT FROM ITS OWN RESOURCE POLICY: max_artifact_bytes applied only to artifacts fetched through the CAS, so a 9.4 MB root verified under an 8 MiB ceiling. And claim.operands was unbounded while references.operands was not; both planes are bounded before either is iterated.

JCS gate widened: 4 positive vectors (adding ES6 number boundaries as STATED rather than derived expectations, so they are usable by a non-JavaScript implementation), 5 encoder negatives and 4 wire negatives. Still NOT the reference suite, and full conformance is still not claimed.
changelog_from_1_53_0: law:proof.canonical-wire@1 — P4's artifact_root hashed the PARSED object, so it was not a byte address. Pretty and compact encodings shared a root, and a DUPLICATE `protocol` member — which JSON.parse resolves in favour of the last one — let bytes containing TRVM-EVIL-v1 be AUTHENTICATED as the honest artifact at ok:true with zero refusals. Resolution now requires received_bytes === canonicalWire(parsed) before it hashes anything.

THE TREE HAS ONE CANONICAL ENCODER AND IT IS NOW MEASURED AGAINST THE STANDARD. canonicalWire IS canonicalBytes, and jcs_vectors.mjs runs it against three published RFC 8785 vectors including the UTF-16 CODE-UNIT ordering case where U+1F602 must precede U+FB33 — the vector a code-point implementation fails and every surrogate-free vector misses. law:proof.reference-is-not-claim@1 — artifact_root sat inside claim.operands and therefore inside nested_claim_sem_id, so rewording one English annotation on a leaf renamed the theorem at every level above it. The artifact is now five planes: claim, chain_ids, references, aggregate (evidence) and structure (DAG shape), with the VERIFIER EXECUTION plane not in the artifact at all. Protocol revised to TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v2.

OPERATIONAL COUNTS LEFT THE ARTIFACT. child_checker_invocations was in the aggregate and child_verdicts_cached_across_citations was in the claim scope, so a sound verifier switching from repeated evaluation to run-local reuse would have renamed the theorem. What an artifact may state about its own shape is strategy-independent: films_below_by_edge_multiplicity (404) and films_below_distinct (138) are both structural; how many the verifier actually replayed is not.

GPT's Q1 RULING TAKEN, AND P4 WAS WRONG IN THE CAUTIOUS DIRECTION. A memo created inside one top-level verification, populated only by this verifier, keyed by an immutable snapshot it owns, never persisted and never transmitted, is DERIVATION REUSE rather than a warrant — nothing crosses an authority boundary. Measured observationally equivalent on an honest DAG AND a forged one: 4 evaluations + 2 reuses = 6 walked with reuse, 8 + 0 = 8 without, identical verdicts and identical refusal sets.

law:proof.verifier-policy-owned@1 — the shipped depth ceiling was an ordinary argument. checkNestBundle(chain40, {store, max_depth: 1000}) returned VERIFIED over the 40-deep chain P4 shipped as its own positive witness for that guard. A caller may now only tighten; a weakening request is refused nest-policy-weakened and the effective policy's id is reported beside the verdict.

A CEILING ON CITATION CHAINS IS ABOUT HEIGHT, NOT RECURSION DEPTH — found by the tightening test, which is the half of the property nobody would have thought to check. The resolver only descends into COMPOSED artifacts, so on D→C2→C1→A it reached depth 2 while the height is 3, and max_depth:2 accepted a DAG taller than its own bound.

AN UNTRUSTED CITATION MAY NOT STEER A FILESYSTEM READ. directoryStore built join(dir, root + '.json') from whatever string arrived, so get('../proof_bundle') returned 1.31 MB from outside the store before the root comparison rejected it: integrity caught the wrong artifact and nothing caught the traversal. ^root-[0-9a-f]{64}$ is checked before a root reaches a path, a store or a hash.

P1 AND P2 COMPARED RECEIPTS WITH JSON.stringify, WHICH IS KEY-ORDER SENSITIVE, and the canonical-wire ruling walked straight into it: storing the P1 bundle canonically sorts its keys, and its own checker then refused it with proof-receipt-replaced on every case. Semantically identical, serially different. Any independently implemented producer emitting another key order would have hit exactly this. The comparisons are canonical now; no identity moved, because the identities already ran through canonicalBytes.

THE CYCLE CLAIM IS STATED AS THE BOUNDED EXPERIMENT IT IS. 512 attempted fixpoints producing 512 distinct roots is evidence that a cycle was not sealable, not a proof that SHA-256 has no fixed point for this encoding. nest-cycle is kept, is defence in depth, and is not load-bearing.
changelog_from_1_52_0: law:proof.content-address-is-not-a-warrant@1 — IDENTITY, AVAILABILITY, WARRANT. P3 carried its children whole (1.6 MB for two). P4 names them by content address, resolves them from a store it does not trust, re-derives the root from the parsed object, and STILL runs every child's own checker on every citation. The saving is entirely in storage and the measurement says so: 8 invocations over 4 distinct artifacts.

A COMPOSED CERTIFICATE WAS NOT CITABLE, and this was measured rather than assumed. verifiedClaimSemId binds protocol, claim, aggregate and CHAIN; the shipped P3 artifact has no chain_ids, so naming it THREW `certificate-incomplete: chain_ids`. P3's non-transitivity was a hole, not a policy. There is a fourth thing before identity/availability/warrant, and it is CITABILITY.

A COMPOSITION'S CHAIN IS DERIVED FROM ITS CHILDREN AND MAY NOT BE DECLARED. chain_ids(composed) = the flat, deduplicated set of its direct children's chain records — O(distinct compilers), not O(evidence), so it never grows with depth and the parent still reads only its direct children. A producer that wrote its own would be naming the compiler its own proof was checked against.

cas.mjs is a new evidence class and its narrowest property is the point: a store may be asked only `do you have bytes under this name` and may answer only with bytes. There is no verify(), no verdict and no accepted-set in it. The root is taken over the PARSED OBJECT rather than the received octets, so a JSON duplicate key cannot make the thing authenticated and the thing reasoned about two different values.

THE DEPTH CEILING HAS A POSITIVE WITNESS AT ITS SHIPPED VALUE — a real 40-deep citation chain, every node sealed and stored, refused at 32 without reaching a leaf. The cycle guard does NOT: sealing a cycle needs bytes that hash to a root those bytes already cite, and 512 attempted fixpoints produced 512 distinct roots. It is declared defence in depth rather than asserted unreachable.

A VERDICT IS ONE ANSWER AND A DIAGNOSIS IS NOT. The first version of the nest checker answered a 40-deep chain refused by its own ceiling with nothing but `nest-child-refused`, and the case written to witness the ceiling failed because the code it names never reached the top. Refusal codes are accumulated through the recursion and reported as a derived measurement beside the verdict.

UNDER CONTENT ADDRESSING THERE IS NO STALENESS, ONLY VERSIONS. P3 measured that rewording unbound prose leaves a citation intact; measured here, rewording a child holds its verified_claim_sem_id and MOVES its artifact_root. An operand therefore carries one stable name and one brittle one, answering different questions — and nothing breaks, because the old bytes are still in the store under the old root.
changelog_from_1_51_0: law:proof.semantic-vocabulary-closed@1 — AUTHENTICATION IS NOT VERIFICATION. Three rounds of repair (P1.1 scope, P2.1 absence contract, P3 citation semantics) each stopped the claimant defining a semantics and each owned the VALUES OF KNOWN FIELDS rather than the FIELD SET. schema.mjs is a new evidence class: one primitive (grammar) and no schemas. Every protocol's key sets are declared inside that protocol's checker and NOT imported, which is the same rule as IMPLEMENTED_SCOPE, IMPLEMENTED_REFUSAL_CONTRACT and IMPLEMENTED_CHILD_PROTOCOLS.

publicResult makes ok === (verdict === VERIFIED) structural on all three checkers; the old distinction survives as evidence_verdict.

experiment_falsifiers.mjs — the control plane is ATTACKED, not described: ten cases including the dry run, restoring the run record and leaving no receipts, verified by digest.

TRVM-BLIND-IMPLEMENTATION-RUN-v3 and TRVM-BLIND-RUN-RECEIPT-v2. TRVM-BLIND-RUN-RESULT-v3. EXPERIMENT-FALSIFIERS 18 -> 21: R is the bypass, S the honest completion that must keep working, T the five ways evidence loss and tampering must become visible — plus the control that a REVEALED run has no RESULT and stays valid.

changelog_from_1_65_0: law:proof.evidence-shape-unambiguous@1 — RESULT and receipt collections keyed by implementation collapsed duplicates with the last row winning, so a bogus row inserted FIRST left BLIND-RUN green while a reader resolving by first occurrence saw a different measurement. P4.1's duplicate wire member, in an array. Uniqueness and label shape are checked before any collection is indexed, and an ambiguous artifact is refused before anything else is attempted.

Every RESULT and receipt shape is CLOSED, every member DERIVED / CHECKED / NON_AUTHORITATIVE. changelog_from_1_68_0: law:proof.mount-is-a-private-object@1 -- the mount was closed as a FILE SET and bypassed four ways without a package byte being wrong: an empty directory is invisible to every digest, the mount ROOT was never lstat'ed, and a hard link to identical bytes verified clean and then mutated through the other name. The directory namespace is derived from the file namespace, the root is lstat'ed before it is read, nlink === 1 is required, path segments are portable and case-fold-unique, and the harness serves the bytes it verified out of a private tmpfs in an unshared mount namespace rather than a path it re-resolves.

verifyPackageAt() walked the tree, walked it AGAIN inside computePackageAt(), and re-read every .json a third time -- three observations of a mutable filesystem at three instants -- then compared two of those counts and called it 'derived on both sides, so exactly these files is arithmetic'. It was ONE FUNCTION CALLED TWICE, which is verbatim the P4.7.8 finding that three checks agreed because all three were one check called three times. One walk now, and the bytes it read are what everything downstream uses.
`--verify-mount --expect <bpkg>` removed. It let the CALLER name the identity the mount is checked against, and nothing in the tree ever passed it.

The blind contract told a harness to verify the mount and then mount it read-only -- the sequence GPT proved insufficient. Sections 2.0 and 2.0.1 state what the mount is and what makes it private. Experiment revision 10.
